texts.1co.5.6: Your boasting [is] not good. Do ye not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?
texts.1co.5.7: Purge out the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, according as ye are unleavened. For also our passover, Christ, has been sacrificed;
texts.1co.5.8: so that let us celebrate the feast, not with old leaven, nor with leaven of malice and wickedness, but with unleavened [bread] of sincerity and truth.
texts.1co.5.9: I have written to you in the epistle not to mix with fornicators;
texts.1co.5.10: not altogether with the fornicators of this world, or with the avaricious and rapacious, or idolaters, since [then] ye should go out of the world.
texts.1co.5.11: But now I have written to you, if any one called brother be fornicator, or avaricious, or idolater, or abusive, or a drunkard, or rapacious, not to mix with [him]; with such a one not even to eat.
texts.1co.5.12: For what have *I* [to do] with judging those outside also? *ye*, do not ye judge them that are within?
texts.1co.5.13: But those without God judges. Remove the wicked person from amongst yourselves.
texts.1co.6.1: Dare any one of you, having a matter against another, prosecute his suit before the unjust, and not before the saints?
texts.1co.6.2: Do ye not then know that the saints shall judge the world? and if the world is judged by you, are ye unworthy of [the] smallest judgments?
texts.1co.6.3: Do ye not know that we shall judge angels? and not then matters of this life?
texts.1co.6.4: If then ye have judgments as to things of this life, set those [to judge] who are little esteemed in the assembly.
texts.1co.6.5: I speak to you [to put you] to shame. Thus there is not a wise person among you, not even one, who shall be able to decide between his brethren!
texts.1co.6.6: But brother prosecutes his suit with brother, and that before unbelievers.
texts.1co.6.7: Already indeed then it is altogether a fault in you that ye have suits between yourselves. Why do ye not rather suffer wrong? why are ye not rather defrauded?
texts.1co.6.8: But *ye* do wrong, and defraud, and this [your] brethren.
texts.1co.6.9: Do ye not know that unrighteous [persons] shall not inherit [the] kingdom of God? Do not err: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor those who make women of themselves, nor who abuse themselves with men,
texts.1co.6.10: nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor abusive persons, nor [the] rapacious, shall inherit [the] kingdom of God.
texts.1co.6.11: And these things were some of you; but ye have been washed, but ye have been sanctified, but ye have been justified in the name of the Lord Jesus, and by the Spirit of our God.
texts.1co.6.12: All things are lawful to me, but all things do not profit; all things are lawful to me, but *I* will not be brought under the power of any.
texts.1co.6.13: Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats; but God will bring to nothing both it and them: but the body [is] not for fornication, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
texts.1co.6.14: And God has both raised up the Lord, and will raise us up from among [the dead] by his power.
texts.1co.6.15: Do ye not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then, taking the members of the Christ, make [them] members of a harlot? Far be the thought.
texts.1co.6.16: Do ye not know that he [that is] joined to the harlot is one body? for the two, he says, shall be one flesh.
texts.1co.6.17: But he that [is] joined to the Lord is one Spirit.
texts.1co.6.18: Flee fornication. Every sin which a man may practise is without the body, but he that commits fornication sins against his own body.
texts.1co.6.19: Do ye not know that your body is [the] temple of the Holy Spirit which [is] in you, which ye have of God; and ye are not your own?
texts.1co.6.20: for ye have been bought with a price: glorify now then God in your body.
texts.1co.7.1: But concerning the things of which ye have written [to me]: [It is] good for a man not to touch a woman;
texts.1co.7.2: but on account of fornications, let each have his own wife, and each [woman] have her own husband.
texts.1co.7.3: Let the husband render her due to the wife, and in like manner the wife to the husband.
texts.1co.7.4: The wife has not authority over her own body, but the husband: in like manner also the husband has not authority over his own body, but the wife.
texts.1co.7.5: Defraud not one another, unless, it may be, by consent for a time, that ye may devote yourselves to prayer, and again be together, that Satan tempt you not because of your incontinency.
texts.1co.7.6: But this I say, as consenting [to], not as commanding [it].
texts.1co.7.7: Now I wish all men to be even as myself: but every one has his own gift of God: one man thus, and another thus.
texts.1co.7.8: But I say to the unmarried and to the widows, It is good for them that they remain even as I.
texts.1co.7.9: But if they have not control over themselves, let them marry; for it is better to marry than to burn.
texts.1co.7.10: But to the married I enjoin, not *I*, but the Lord, Let not wife be separated from husband;
texts.1co.7.11: (but if also she shall have been separated, let her remain unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband;) and let not husband leave wife.
texts.1co.7.12: But as to the rest, *I* say, not the Lord, If any brother have an unbelieving wife, and *she* consent to dwell with him, let him not leave her.
texts.1co.7.13: And a woman who has an unbelieving husband, and he consents to dwell with her, let her not leave [her] husband.
texts.1co.7.14: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the brother; since [otherwise] indeed your children are unclean, but now they are holy.
texts.1co.7.15: But if the unbeliever go away, let them go away; a brother or a sister is not bound in such [cases], but God has called us in peace.
texts.1co.7.16: For what knowest thou, O wife, if thou shalt save thy husband? or what knowest thou, O husband, if thou shalt save thy wife?
texts.1co.7.17: However, as the Lord has divided to each, as God has called each, so let him walk; and thus I ordain in all the assemblies.
texts.1co.7.18: Has any one been called circumcised? let him not become uncircumcised: has any one been called in uncircumcision? let him not be circumcised.
texts.1co.7.19: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing; but keeping God's commandments.
texts.1co.7.20: Let each abide in that calling in which he has been called.
texts.1co.7.21: Hast thou been called [being] a bondman, let it not concern thee; but and if thou canst become free, use [it] rather.
texts.1co.7.22: For the bondman that is called in [the] Lord is the Lord's freedman; in like manner [also] the freeman being called is Christ's bondman.
texts.1co.7.23: Ye have been bought with a price; do not be the bondmen of men.
texts.1co.7.24: Let each, wherein he is called, brethren, therein abide with God.
texts.1co.7.25: But concerning virgins, I have no commandment of [the] Lord; but I give my opinion, as having received mercy of [the] Lord to be faithful.
texts.1co.7.26: I think then that this is good, on account of the present necessity, that [it is] good for a man to remain so as he is.
texts.1co.7.27: Art thou bound to a wife? seek not to be loosed; art thou free from a wife? do not seek a wife.
texts.1co.7.28: But if thou shouldest also marry, thou hast not sinned; and if the virgin marry, they have not sinned: but such shall have tribulation in the flesh; but I spare you.
texts.1co.7.29: But this I say, brethren, the time is straitened. For the rest, that they who have wives, be as not having [any]:
texts.1co.7.30: and they that weep, as not weeping; and they that rejoice, as not rejoicing; and they that buy, as not possessing;
texts.1co.7.31: and they that use the world, as not disposing of it as their own; for the fashion of this world passes.
texts.1co.7.32: But I wish you to be without care. The unmarried cares for the things of the Lord, how he shall please the Lord;
texts.1co.7.33: but he that has married cares for the things of the world, how he shall please his wife.
texts.1co.7.34: There is a difference between the wife and the virgin. The unmarried cares for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and spirit; but she that has married cares for the things of the world, how she shall please her husband.
texts.1co.7.35: But I say this for your own profit; not that I may set a snare before you, but for what [is] seemly, and waiting on the Lord without distraction.
texts.1co.7.36: But if any one think that he behaves unseemly to his virginity, if he be beyond the flower of his age, and so it must be, let him do what he will, he does not sin: let them marry.
texts.1co.7.37: But he who stands firm in his heart, having no need, but has authority over his own will, and has judged this in his heart to keep his own virginity, he does well.
texts.1co.7.38: So that he that marries himself does well; and he that does not marry does better.
texts.1co.7.39: A wife is bound for whatever time her husband lives; but if the husband be fallen asleep, she is free to be married to whom she will, only in [the] Lord.
texts.1co.7.40: But she is happier if she so remain, according to my judgment; but I think that *I* also have God's Spirit.
texts.1co.8.1: But concerning things sacrificed to idols, we know, (for we all have knowledge: knowledge puffs up, but love edifies.
texts.1co.8.2: If any one think he knows anything, he knows nothing yet as he ought to know [it].
texts.1co.8.3: But if any one love God, *he* is known of him):
texts.1co.8.4: -- concerning then the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol [is] nothing in [the] world, and that there [is] no other God save one.
texts.1co.8.5: For and if indeed there are [those] called gods, whether in heaven or on earth, (as there are gods many, and lords many,)
texts.1co.8.6: yet to us [there is] one God, the Father, of whom all things, and *we* for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, by whom [are] all things, and *we* by him.
texts.1co.8.7: But knowledge [is] not in all: but some, with conscience of the idol, until now eat as of a thing sacrificed to idols; and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
texts.1co.8.8: But meat does not commend us to God; neither if we should not eat do we come short; nor if we should eat have we an advantage.
texts.1co.8.9: But see lest anywise this your right [to eat] itself be a stumbling-block to the weak.
texts.1co.8.10: For if any one see thee, who hast knowledge, sitting at table in an idol-house, shall not his conscience, he being weak, be emboldened to eat the things sacrificed to the idol?
texts.1co.8.11: and the weak [one], the brother for whose sake Christ died, will perish through thy knowledge.
texts.1co.8.12: Now, thus sinning against the brethren, and wounding their weak conscience, ye sin against Christ.
texts.1co.8.13: Wherefore if meat be a fall-trap to my brother, I will eat no flesh for ever, that I may not be a fall-trap to my brother.
texts.1co.9.1: Am I not free? am I not an apostle? have I not seen Jesus our Lord? are not *ye* my work in [the] Lord?
texts.1co.9.2: If I am not an apostle to others, yet at any rate I am to you: for the seal of mine apostleship are *ye* in [the] Lord.
texts.1co.9.3: My defence to those who examine me is this:
texts.1co.9.4: Have we not a right to eat and to drink?
texts.1co.9.5: have we not a right to take round a sister [as] wife, as also the other apostles, and the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas?
texts.1co.9.6: Or *I* alone and Barnabas, have we not a right not to work?
texts.1co.9.7: Who ever carries on war at his own charges? who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? or who herds a flock and does not eat of the milk of the flock?
texts.1co.9.8: Do I speak these things as a man, or does not the law also say these things?
texts.1co.9.9: For in the law of Moses it is written, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that is treading out corn. Is God occupied about the oxen,
texts.1co.9.10: or does he say [it] altogether for our sakes? For for our sakes it has been written, that the plougher should plough in hope, and he that treads out corn, in hope of partaking of [it].
texts.1co.9.11: If we have sown to you spiritual things, [is it a] great [thing] if *we* shall reap your carnal things?
texts.1co.9.12: If others partake of this right over you, should not rather *we*? But we have not used this right, but we bear all things, that we may put no hindrance in the way of the glad tidings of the Christ.
texts.1co.9.13: Do ye not know that they who labour [at] sacred things eat of the [offerings offered in the] temple; they that attend at the altar partake with the altar?
texts.1co.9.14: So also the Lord has ordained to those that announce the glad tidings to live of the glad tidings.
texts.1co.9.15: But *I* have used none of these things. Now I have not written these things that it should be thus in my case; for [it were] good for me rather to die than that any one should make vain my boast.
texts.1co.9.16: For if I announce the glad tidings, I have nothing to boast of; for a necessity is laid upon me; for it is woe to me if I should not announce the glad tidings.
texts.1co.9.17: For if I do this voluntarily, I have a reward; but if not of my own will, I am entrusted with an administration.
texts.1co.9.18: What is the reward then that I have? That in announcing the glad tidings I make the glad tidings costless [to others], so as not to have made use, as belonging to me, of my right in [announcing] the glad tidings.
texts.1co.9.19: For being free from all, I have made myself bondman to all, that I might gain the most [possible].
texts.1co.9.20: And I became to the Jews as a Jew, in order that I might gain the Jews: to those under law, as under law, not being myself under law, in order that I might gain those under law:
texts.1co.9.21: to those without law, as without law, (not as without law to God, but as legitimately subject to Christ,) in order that I might gain [those] without law.
texts.1co.9.22: I became to the weak, [as] weak, in order that I might gain the weak. To all I have become all things, in order that at all events I might save some.
texts.1co.9.23: And I do all things for the sake of the glad tidings, that I may be fellow-partaker with them.
texts.1co.9.24: Know ye not that they who run in [the] race-course run all, but one receives the prize? Thus run in order that ye may obtain.
texts.1co.9.25: But every one that contends [for a prize] is temperate in all things: *they* then indeed that they may receive a corruptible crown, but *we* an incorruptible.
texts.1co.9.26: *I* therefore thus run, as not uncertainly; so I combat, as not beating the air.
texts.1co.9.27: But I buffet my body, and lead it captive, lest [after] having preached to others I should be myself rejected.
texts.1co.10.1: For I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;
texts.1co.10.2: and all were baptised unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
texts.1co.10.3: and all ate the same spiritual food,
texts.1co.10.4: and all drank the same spiritual drink, for they drank of a spiritual rock which followed [them]: (now the rock was the Christ;)
texts.1co.10.5: yet God was not pleased with the most of them, for they were strewed in the desert.
texts.1co.10.6: But these things happened [as] types of us, that we should not be lusters after evil things, as they also lusted.
texts.1co.10.7: Neither be ye idolaters, as some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.
texts.1co.10.8: Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed fornication, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.
texts.1co.10.9: Neither let us tempt the Christ, as some of them tempted, and perished by serpents.
texts.1co.10.10: Neither murmur ye, as some of them murmured, and perished by the destroyer.
texts.1co.10.11: Now all these things happened to them [as] types, and have been written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the ages are come.
texts.1co.10.12: So that let him that thinks that he stands take heed lest he fall.
texts.1co.10.13: No temptation has taken you but such as is according to man's nature; and God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above what ye are able [to bear], but will with the temptation make the issue also, so that [ye] should be able to bear [it].
texts.1co.10.14: Wherefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
texts.1co.10.15: I speak as to intelligent [persons]: do *ye* judge what I say.
texts.1co.10.16: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not [the] communion of the blood of the Christ? The bread which we break, is it not [the] communion of the body of the Christ?
texts.1co.10.17: Because we, [being] many, are one loaf, one body; for we all partake of that one loaf.
texts.1co.10.18: See Israel according to flesh: are not they who eat the sacrifices in communion with the altar?
texts.1co.10.19: What then do I say? that what is sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
texts.1co.10.20: But that what [the nations] sacrifice they sacrifice to demons, and not to God. Now I do not wish you to be in communion with demons.
texts.1co.10.21: Ye cannot drink [the] Lord's cup, and [the] cup of demons: ye cannot partake of [the] Lord's table, and of [the] table of demons.
texts.1co.10.22: Do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? are we stronger than he?
texts.1co.10.23: All things are lawful, but all are not profitable; all things are lawful, but all do not edify.
texts.1co.10.24: Let no one seek his own [advantage], but that of the other.
texts.1co.10.25: Everything sold in the shambles eat, making no inquiry for conscience sake.
texts.1co.10.26: For the earth [is] the Lord's and its fulness.
texts.1co.10.27: But if any one of the unbelievers invite you, and ye are minded to go, all that is set before you eat, making no inquiry for conscience sake.
texts.1co.10.28: But if any one say to you, This is offered to holy purposes, do not eat, for his sake that pointed it out, and conscience sake;
texts.1co.10.29: but conscience, I mean, not thine own, but that of the other: for why is my liberty judged by another conscience?
texts.1co.10.30: If *I* partake with thanksgiving, why am I spoken evil of for what *I* give thanks for?
texts.1co.10.31: Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatever ye do, do all things to God's glory.
texts.1co.10.32: Give no occasion to stumbling, whether to Jews, or Greeks, or the assembly of God.
texts.1co.10.33: Even as *I* also please all in all things; not seeking my own profit, but that of the many, that they may be saved.
texts.1co.11.1: Be my imitators, even as *I* also [am] of Christ.
texts.1co.11.2: Now I praise you, that in all things ye are mindful of me; and that as I have directed you, ye keep the directions.
texts.1co.11.3: But I wish you to know that the Christ is the head of every man, but woman's head [is] the man, and the Christ's head God.
texts.1co.11.4: Every man praying or prophesying, having [anything] on his head, puts his head to shame.
texts.1co.11.5: But every woman praying or prophesying with her head uncovered puts her own head to shame; for it is one and the same as a shaved [woman].
texts.1co.11.6: For if a woman be not covered, let her hair also be cut off. But if [it be] shameful to a woman to have her hair cut off or to be shaved, let her be covered.
texts.1co.11.7: For man indeed ought not to have his head covered, being God's image and glory; but woman is man's glory.
texts.1co.11.8: For man is not of woman, but woman of man.
texts.1co.11.9: For also man was not created for the sake of the woman, but woman for the sake of the man.
texts.1co.11.10: Therefore ought the woman to have authority on her head, on account of the angels.
texts.1co.11.11: However, neither [is] woman without man, nor man without woman, in [the] Lord.
texts.1co.11.12: For as the woman [is] of the man, so also [is] the man by the woman, but all things of God.
texts.1co.11.13: Judge in yourselves: is it comely that a woman should pray to God uncovered?
texts.1co.11.14: Does not even nature itself teach you, that man, if he have long hair, it is a dishonour to him?
texts.1co.11.15: But woman, if she have long hair, [it is] glory to her; for the long hair is given [to her] in lieu of a veil.
texts.1co.11.16: But if any one think to be contentious, *we* have no such custom, nor the assemblies of God.
texts.1co.11.17: But [in] prescribing [to you on] this [which I now enter on], I do not praise, [namely,] that ye come together, not for the better, but for the worse.
texts.1co.11.18: For first, when ye come together in assembly, I hear there exist divisions among you, and I partly give credit [to it].
texts.1co.11.19: For there must also be sects among you, that the approved may become manifest among you.
texts.1co.11.20: When ye come therefore together into one place, it is not to eat [the] Lord's supper.
texts.1co.11.21: For each one in eating takes his *own* supper before [others], and one is hungry and another drinks to excess.
texts.1co.11.22: Have ye not then houses for eating and drinking? or do ye despise the assembly of God, and put to shame them who have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you? In this [point] I do not praise.
texts.1co.11.23: For *I* received from the Lord, that which I also delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus, in the night in which he was delivered up, took bread,
texts.1co.11.24: and having given thanks broke [it], and said, This is my body, which [is] for you: this do in remembrance of me.
texts.1co.11.25: In like manner also the cup, after having supped, saying, This cup is the new covenant in my blood: this do, as often as ye shall drink [it], in remembrance of me.
texts.1co.11.26: For as often as ye shall eat this bread, and drink the cup, ye announce the death of the Lord, until he come.
texts.1co.11.27: So that whosoever shall eat the bread, or drink the cup of the Lord, unworthily, shall be guilty in respect of the body and of the blood of the Lord.
texts.1co.11.28: But let a man prove himself, and thus eat of the bread, and drink of the cup.
texts.1co.11.29: For [the] eater and drinker eats and drinks judgment to himself, not distinguishing the body.
texts.1co.11.30: On this account many among you [are] weak and infirm, and a good many are fallen asleep.
texts.1co.11.31: But if we judged ourselves, so were we not judged.
texts.1co.11.32: But being judged, we are disciplined of [the] Lord, that we may not be condemned with the world.
texts.1co.11.33: So that, my brethren, when ye come together to eat, wait for one another.
texts.1co.11.34: If any one be hungry, let him eat at home, that ye may not come together for judgment. But the other things, whenever I come, I will set in order.
texts.1co.12.1: But concerning spiritual [manifestations], brethren, I do not wish you to be ignorant.
texts.1co.12.2: Ye know that when ye were [of the] nations [ye were] led away to dumb idols, in whatever way ye might be led.
texts.1co.12.3: I give you therefore to know, that no one, speaking in [the power of the] Spirit of God, says, Curse [on] Jesus; and no one can say, Lord Jesus, unless in [the power of the] Holy Spirit.
texts.1co.12.4: But there are distinctions of gifts, but the same Spirit;
texts.1co.12.5: and there are distinctions of services, and the same Lord;
texts.1co.12.6: and there are distinctions of operations, but the same God who operates all things in all.
texts.1co.12.7: But to each the manifestation of the Spirit is given for profit.
texts.1co.12.8: For to one, by the Spirit, is given [the] word of wisdom; and to another [the] word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit;
texts.1co.12.9: and to a different one faith, in [the power of] the same Spirit; and to another gifts of healing in [the power of] the same Spirit;
texts.1co.12.10: and to another operations of miracles; and to another prophecy; and to another discerning of spirits; and to a different one kinds of tongues; and to another interpretation of tongues.
texts.1co.12.11: But all these things operates the one and the same Spirit, dividing to each in particular according as he pleases.
texts.1co.12.12: For even as the body is one and has many members, but all the members of the body, being many, are one body, so also [is] the Christ.
texts.1co.12.13: For also in [the power of] one Spirit *we* have all been baptised into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, whether bondmen or free, and have all been given to drink of one Spirit.
texts.1co.12.14: For also the body is not one member but many.
texts.1co.12.15: If the foot say, Because I am not a hand I am not of the body, is it on account of this not indeed of the body?
texts.1co.12.16: And if the ear say, Because I am not an eye I am not of the body, is it on account of this not indeed of the body?
texts.1co.12.17: If the whole body [were] an eye, where the hearing? if all hearing, where the smelling?
texts.1co.12.18: But now God has set the members, each one of them in the body, according as it has pleased [him].
texts.1co.12.19: But if all were one member, where the body?
texts.1co.12.20: But now the members [are] many, and the body one.
texts.1co.12.21: The eye cannot say to the hand, I have not need of thee; or again, the head to the feet, I have not need of you.
texts.1co.12.22: But much rather, the members of the body which seem to be weaker are necessary;
texts.1co.12.23: and those [parts] of the body which we esteem to be the more void of honour, these we clothe with more abundant honour; and our uncomely [parts] have more abundant comeliness;
texts.1co.12.24: but our comely [parts] have not need. But God has tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to [the part] that lacked;
texts.1co.12.25: that there might be no division in the body, but that the members might have the same concern one for another.
texts.1co.12.26: And if one member suffer, all the members suffer with [it]; and if one member be glorified, all the members rejoice with [it].
texts.1co.12.27: Now *ye* are Christ's body, and members in particular.
texts.1co.12.28: And God has set certain in the assembly: first, apostles; secondly, prophets; thirdly, teachers; then miraculous powers; then gifts of healings; helps; governments; kinds of tongues.
texts.1co.12.29: [Are] all apostles? [are] all prophets? [are] all teachers? [are] all [in possession of] miraculous powers?
texts.1co.12.30: have all gifts of healings? do all speak with tongues? do all interpret?
texts.1co.12.31: But desire earnestly the greater gifts, and yet shew I unto you a way of more surpassing excellence.
texts.1co.13.1: If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.
texts.1co.13.2: And if I have prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.
texts.1co.13.3: And if I shall dole out all my goods in food, and if I deliver up my body that I may be burned, but have not love, I profit nothing.
texts.1co.13.4: Love has long patience, is kind; love is not emulous [of others]; love is not insolent and rash, is not puffed up,
texts.1co.13.5: does not behave in an unseemly manner, does not seek what is its own, is not quickly provoked, does not impute evil,
texts.1co.13.6: does not rejoice at iniquity but rejoices with the truth,
texts.1co.13.7: bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
texts.1co.13.8: Love never fails; but whether prophecies, they shall be done away; or tongues, they shall cease; or knowledge, it shall be done away.
texts.1co.13.9: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part:
texts.1co.13.10: but when that which is perfect has come, that which is in part shall be done away.
texts.1co.13.11: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I felt as a child, I reasoned as a child; when I became a man, I had done with what belonged to the child.
texts.1co.13.12: For we see now through a dim window obscurely, but then face to face; now I know partially, but then I shall know according as I also have been known.
texts.1co.13.13: And now abide faith, hope, love; these three things; and the greater of these [is] love.
texts.1co.14.1: Follow after love, and be emulous of spiritual [manifestations], but rather that ye may prophesy.
texts.1co.14.2: For he that speaks with a tongue does not speak to men but to God: for no one hears; but in spirit he speaks mysteries.
texts.1co.14.3: But he that prophesies speaks to men [in] edification, and encouragement, and consolation.
texts.1co.14.4: He that speaks with a tongue edifies himself; but he that prophesies edifies [the] assembly.
texts.1co.14.5: Now I desire that ye should all speak with tongues, but rather that ye should prophesy. But greater is he that prophesies than he that speaks with tongues, unless he interpret, that the assembly may receive edification.
texts.1co.14.6: And now, brethren, if I come to you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, unless I shall speak to you either in revelation, or in knowledge, or in prophecy, or in teaching?
texts.1co.14.7: Even lifeless things giving a sound, whether pipe or harp, if they give not distinction to the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped?
texts.1co.14.8: For also, if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself for war?
texts.1co.14.9: Thus also *ye* with the tongue, unless ye give a distinct speech, how shall it be known what is spoken? for ye will be speaking to the air.
texts.1co.14.10: There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and none of undistinguishable sound.
texts.1co.14.11: If therefore I do not know the power of the sound, I shall be to him that speaks a barbarian, and he that speaks a barbarian for me.
texts.1co.14.12: Thus *ye* also, since ye are desirous of spirits, seek that ye may abound for the edification of the assembly.
texts.1co.14.13: Wherefore let him that speaks with a tongue pray that he may interpret.
texts.1co.14.14: For if I pray with a tongue, my spirit prays, but my understanding is unfruitful.
texts.1co.14.15: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, but I will pray also with the understanding; I will sing with the spirit, but I will sing also with the understanding.
texts.1co.14.16: Since otherwise, if thou blessest with [the] spirit, how shall he who fills the place of the simple [Christian] say Amen, at thy giving of thanks, since he does not know what thou sayest?
texts.1co.14.17: For *thou* indeed givest thanks well, but the other is not edified.
texts.1co.14.18: I thank God I speak in a tongue more than all of you:
texts.1co.14.19: but in [the] assembly I desire to speak five words with my understanding, that I may instruct others also, [rather] than ten thousand words in a tongue.
texts.1co.14.20: Brethren, be not children in [your] minds, but in malice be babes; but in [your] minds be grown [men].
texts.1co.14.21: It is written in the law, By people of other tongues, and by strange lips, will I speak to this people; and neither thus will they hear me, saith the Lord.
texts.1co.14.22: So that tongues are for a sign, not to those who believe, but to unbelievers; but prophecy, not to unbelievers, but to those who believe.
texts.1co.14.23: If therefore the whole assembly come together in one place, and all speak with tongues, and simple [persons] enter in, or unbelievers, will not they say ye are mad?
texts.1co.14.24: But if all prophesy, and some unbeliever or simple [person] come in, he is convicted of all, he is judged of all;
texts.1co.14.25: the secrets of his heart are manifested; and thus, falling upon [his] face, he will do homage to God, reporting that God is indeed amongst you.
texts.1co.14.26: What is it then, brethren? whenever ye come together, each [of you] has a psalm, has a teaching, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation. Let all things be done to edification.
texts.1co.14.27: If any one speak with a tongue, [let it be] two, or at the most three, and separately, and let one interpret;
texts.1co.14.28: but if there be no interpreter, let him be silent in [the] assembly, and let him speak to himself and to God.
texts.1co.14.29: And let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge.
texts.1co.14.30: But if there be a revelation to another sitting [there], let the first be silent.
texts.1co.14.31: For ye can all prophesy one by one, that all may learn and all be encouraged.
texts.1co.14.32: And spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
texts.1co.14.33: For God is not [a God] of disorder but of peace, as in all the assemblies of the saints.
texts.1co.14.34: Let [your] women be silent in the assemblies, for it is not permitted to them to speak; but to be in subjection, as the law also says.
texts.1co.14.35: But if they wish to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home; for it is a shame for a woman to speak in assembly.
texts.1co.14.36: Did the word of God go out from you, or did it come to you only?
texts.1co.14.37: If any one thinks himself to be a prophet or spiritual, let him recognise the things that I write to you, that it is [the] Lord's commandment.
texts.1co.14.38: But if any be ignorant, let him be ignorant.
texts.1co.14.39: So that, brethren, desire to prophesy, and do not forbid the speaking with tongues.
texts.1co.14.40: But let all things be done comelily and with order.
texts.1co.15.1: But I make known to you, brethren, the glad tidings which I announced to you, which also ye received, in which also ye stand,
texts.1co.15.2: by which also ye are saved, (if ye hold fast the word which I announced to you as the glad tidings,) unless indeed ye have believed in vain.
texts.1co.15.3: For I delivered to you, in the first place, what also I had received, that Christ died for our sins, according to the scriptures;
texts.1co.15.4: and that he was buried; and that he was raised the third day, according to the scriptures;
texts.1co.15.5: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve.
texts.1co.15.6: Then he appeared to above five hundred brethren at once, of whom the most remain until now, but some also have fallen asleep.
texts.1co.15.7: Then he appeared to James; then to all the apostles;
texts.1co.15.8: and last of all, as to an abortion, he appeared to *me* also.
texts.1co.15.9: For *I* am the least of the apostles, who am not fit to be called apostle, because I have persecuted the assembly of God.
texts.1co.15.10: But by God's grace I am what I am; and his grace, which [was] towards me, has not been vain; but I have laboured more abundantly than they all, but not *I*, but the grace of God which [was] with me.
texts.1co.15.11: Whether, therefore, I or they, thus we preach, and thus ye have believed.
texts.1co.15.12: Now if Christ is preached that he is raised from among [the] dead, how say some among you that there is not a resurrection of [those that are] dead?
texts.1co.15.13: But if there is not a resurrection of [those that are] dead, neither is Christ raised:
texts.1co.15.14: but if Christ is not raised, then, indeed, vain also [is] our preaching, and vain also your faith.
texts.1co.15.15: And we are found also false witnesses of God; for we have witnessed concerning God that he raised the Christ, whom he has not raised if indeed [those that are] dead are not raised.
texts.1co.15.16: For if [those that are] dead are not raised, neither is Christ raised;
texts.1co.15.17: but if Christ be not raised, your faith [is] vain; ye are yet in your sins.
texts.1co.15.18: Then indeed also those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
texts.1co.15.19: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are [the] most miserable of all men.
texts.1co.15.20: (But now Christ is raised from among [the] dead, first-fruits of those fallen asleep.
texts.1co.15.21: For since by man [came] death, by man also resurrection of [those that are] dead.
texts.1co.15.22: For as in the Adam all die, thus also in the Christ all shall be made alive.
texts.1co.15.23: But each in his own rank: [the] first-fruits, Christ; then those that are the Christ's at his coming.
texts.1co.15.24: Then the end, when he gives up the kingdom to him [who is] God and Father; when he shall have annulled all rule and all authority and power.
texts.1co.15.25: For he must reign until he put all enemies under his feet.
texts.1co.15.27: For he has put all things in subjection under his feet. But when he says that all things are put in subjection, [it is] evident that [it is] except him who put all things in subjection to him.
texts.1co.15.28: But when all things shall have been brought into subjection to him, then the Son also himself shall be placed in subjection to him who put all things in subjection to him, that God may be all in all.)
texts.1co.15.29: Since what shall the baptised for the dead do if [those that are] dead rise not at all? why also are they baptised for them?
texts.1co.15.30: Why do *we* also endanger ourselves every hour?
texts.1co.15.31: Daily I die, by your boasting which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
texts.1co.15.32: If, [to speak] after the manner of man, I have fought with beasts in Ephesus, what is the profit to me if [those that are] dead do not rise? let us eat and drink; for to-morrow we die.
texts.1co.15.33: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.
texts.1co.15.34: Awake up righteously, and sin not; for some are ignorant of God: I speak to you as a matter of shame.
texts.1co.15.35: But some one will say, How are the dead raised? and with what body do they come?
texts.1co.15.36: Fool; what *thou* sowest is not quickened unless it die.
texts.1co.15.37: And what thou sowest, thou sowest not the body that shall be, but a bare grain: it may be of wheat, or some one of the rest:
texts.1co.15.38: and God gives to it a body as he has pleased, and to each of the seeds its own body.
texts.1co.15.39: Every flesh [is] not the same flesh, but one [is] of men, and another flesh of beasts, and another [flesh] of birds, and another of fishes.
texts.1co.15.40: And [there are] heavenly bodies, and earthly bodies: but different is the glory of the heavenly, different that of the earthly:
texts.1co.15.41: one [the] sun's glory, and another [the] moon's glory, and another [the] stars' glory; for star differs from star in glory.
texts.1co.15.42: Thus also [is] the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption, it is raised in incorruptibility.
texts.1co.15.43: It is sown in dishonour, it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness, it is raised in power.
texts.1co.15.44: It is sown a natural body, it is raised a spiritual body: if there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual [one].
texts.1co.15.45: Thus also it is written, The first man Adam became a living soul; the last Adam a quickening spirit.
texts.1co.15.46: But that which is spiritual [was] not first, but that which is natural, then that which is spiritual:
texts.1co.15.47: the first man out of [the] earth, made of dust; the second man, out of heaven.
texts.1co.15.48: Such as he made of dust, such also those made of dust; and such as the heavenly [one], such also the heavenly [ones].
texts.1co.15.49: And as we have borne the image of the [one] made of dust, we shall bear also the image of the heavenly [one].
texts.1co.15.50: But this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit God's kingdom, nor does corruption inherit incorruptibility.
texts.1co.15.51: Behold, I tell you a mystery: We shall not all fall asleep, but we shall all be changed,
texts.1co.15.52: in an instant, in [the] twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet; for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and *we* shall be changed.
texts.1co.15.53: For this corruptible must needs put on incorruptibility, and this mortal put on immortality.
texts.1co.15.54: But when this corruptible shall have put on incorruptibility, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall come to pass the word written: Death has been swallowed up in victory.
texts.1co.15.55: Where, O death, [is] thy sting? where, O death, thy victory?
texts.1co.15.56: Now the sting of death [is] sin, and the power of sin the law;
texts.1co.15.57: but thanks to God, who gives us the victory by our Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.1co.15.58: So then, my beloved brethren, be firm, immovable, abounding always in the work of the Lord, knowing that your toil is not in vain in [the] Lord.
texts.1co.16.1: Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I directed the assemblies of Galatia, so do *ye* do also.
texts.1co.16.2: On [the] first of [the] week let each of you put by at home, laying up [in] whatever [degree] he may have prospered, that there may be no collections when I come.
texts.1co.16.3: And when I am arrived, whomsoever ye shall approve, these I will send with letters to carry your bounty to Jerusalem:
texts.1co.16.4: and if it be suitable that *I* also should go, they shall go with me.
texts.1co.16.5: But I will come to you when I shall have gone through Macedonia; for I do go through Macedonia.
texts.1co.16.6: But perhaps I will stay with you, or even winter with you, that *ye* may set me forward wheresoever I may go.
texts.1co.16.7: For I will not see you now in passing, for I hope to remain a certain time with you, if the Lord permit.
texts.1co.16.8: But I remain in Ephesus until Pentecost.
texts.1co.16.9: For a great door is opened to me and an effectual [one], and [the] adversaries many.
texts.1co.16.10: Now if Timotheus come, see that he may be with you without fear; for he works the work of the Lord, even as I.
texts.1co.16.11: Let not therefore any one despise him; but set him forward in peace, that he may come to me; for I expect him with the brethren.
texts.1co.16.12: Now concerning the brother Apollos, I begged him much that he would go to you with the brethren; but it was not at all [his] will to go now; but he will come when he shall have good opportunity.
texts.1co.16.13: Be vigilant; stand fast in the faith; quit yourselves like men; be strong.
texts.1co.16.14: Let all things ye do be done in love.
texts.1co.16.15: But I beseech you, brethren, (ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is the first-fruits of Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the saints for service,)
texts.1co.16.16: that *ye* should also be subject to such, and to every one joined in the work and labouring.
texts.1co.16.17: But I rejoice in the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus; because *they* have supplied what was lacking on your part.
texts.1co.16.18: For they have refreshed my spirit and yours: own therefore such.
texts.1co.16.19: The assemblies of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla, with the assembly in their house, salute you much in [the] Lord.
texts.1co.16.20: All the brethren salute you. Salute one another with a holy kiss.
texts.1co.16.21: The salutation of [me] Paul with my own hand.
texts.1co.16.22: If any one love not the Lord [Jesus Christ] let him be Anathema Maranatha.
texts.1co.16.23: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ [be] with you.
texts.1co.16.24: My love [be] with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.

texts.1co.1.1: Paul, a called apostle of Jesus Christ, through the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother,
texts.1co.1.2: to the assembly of God that is in Corinth, to those sanctified in Christ Jesus, called saints, with all those calling upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place -- both theirs and ours:
texts.1co.1.3: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ!
texts.1co.1.4: I give thanks to my God always concerning you for the grace of God that was given to you in Christ Jesus,
texts.1co.1.5: that in every thing ye were enriched in him, in all discourse and all knowledge,
texts.1co.1.6: according as the testimony of the Christ was confirmed in you,
texts.1co.1.7: so that ye are not behind in any gift, waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
texts.1co.1.8: who also shall confirm you unto the end -- unblamable in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ;
texts.1co.1.9: faithful [is] God, through whom ye were called to the fellowship of His Son Jesus Christ our Lord.
texts.1co.1.10: And I call upon you, brethren, through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that the same thing ye may all say, and there may not be divisions among you, and ye may be perfected in the same mind, and in the same judgment,
texts.1co.1.11: for it was signified to me concerning you, my brethren, by those of Chloe, that contentions are among you;
texts.1co.1.12: and I say this, that each one of you saith, `I, indeed, am of Paul' -- `and I of Apollos,' -- `and I of Cephas,' -- `and I of Christ.'
texts.1co.1.13: Hath the Christ been divided? was Paul crucified for you? or to the name of Paul were ye baptized;
texts.1co.1.14: I give thanks to God that no one of you did I baptize, except Crispus and Gaius --
texts.1co.1.15: that no one may say that to my own name I did baptize;
texts.1co.1.16: and I did baptize also Stephanas' household -- further, I have not known if I did baptize any other.
texts.1co.1.17: For Christ did not send me to baptize, but -- to proclaim good news; not in wisdom of discourse, that the cross of the Christ may not be made of none effect;
texts.1co.1.18: for the word of the cross to those indeed perishing is foolishness, and to us -- those being saved -- it is the power of God,
texts.1co.1.19: for it hath been written, `I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the intelligence of the intelligent I will bring to nought;'
texts.1co.1.20: where [is] the wise? where the scribe? where a disputer of this age? did not God make foolish the wisdom of this world?
texts.1co.1.21: for, seeing in the wisdom of God the world through the wisdom knew not God, it did please God through the foolishness of the preaching to save those believing.
texts.1co.1.22: Since also Jews ask a sign, and Greeks seek wisdom,
texts.1co.1.23: also we -- we preach Christ crucified, to Jews, indeed, a stumbling-block, and to Greeks foolishness,
texts.1co.1.24: and to those called -- both Jews and Greeks -- Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God,
texts.1co.1.25: because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men;
texts.1co.1.26: for see your calling, brethren, that not many [are] wise according to the flesh, not many mighty, not many noble;
texts.1co.1.27: but the foolish things of the world did God choose, that the wise He may put to shame; and the weak things of the world did God choose that He may put to shame the strong;
texts.1co.1.28: and the base things of the world, and the things despised did God choose, and the things that are not, that the things that are He may make useless --
texts.1co.1.29: that no flesh may glory before Him;
texts.1co.1.30: and of Him ye -- ye are in Christ Jesus, who became to us from God wisdom, righteousness also, and sanctification, and redemption,
texts.1co.1.31: that, according as it hath been written, `He who is glorying -- in the Lord let him glory.'
texts.1co.2.1: And I, having come unto you, brethren, came -- not in superiority of discourse or wisdom -- declaring to you the testimony of God,
texts.1co.2.2: for I decided not to know any thing among you, except Jesus Christ, and him crucified;
texts.1co.2.3: and I, in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling, was with you;
texts.1co.2.4: and my word and my preaching was not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power --
texts.1co.2.5: that your faith may not be in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
texts.1co.2.6: And wisdom we speak among the perfect, and wisdom not of this age, nor of the rulers of this age -- of those becoming useless,
texts.1co.2.7: but we speak the hidden wisdom of God in a secret, that God foreordained before the ages to our glory,
texts.1co.2.8: which no one of the rulers of this age did know, for if they had known, the Lord of the glory they would not have crucified;
texts.1co.2.9: but, according as it hath been written, `What eye did not see, and ear did not hear, and upon the heart of man came not up, what God did prepare for those loving Him --'
texts.1co.2.10: but to us did God reveal [them] through His Spirit, for the Spirit all things doth search, even the depths of God,
texts.1co.2.11: for who of men hath known the things of the man, except the spirit of the man that [is] in him? so also the things of God no one hath known, except the Spirit of God.
texts.1co.2.12: And we the spirit of the world did not receive, but the Spirit that [is] of God, that we may know the things conferred by God on us,
texts.1co.2.13: which things also we speak, not in words taught by human wisdom, but in those taught by the Holy Spirit, with spiritual things spiritual things comparing,
texts.1co.2.14: and the natural man doth not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for to him they are foolishness, and he is not able to know [them], because spiritually they are discerned;
texts.1co.2.15: and he who is spiritual, doth discern indeed all things, and he himself is by no one discerned;
texts.1co.2.16: for who did know the mind of the Lord that he shall instruct Him? and we -- we have the mind of Christ.
texts.1co.3.1: And I, brethren, was not able to speak to you as to spiritual, but as to fleshly -- as to babes in Christ;
texts.1co.3.2: with milk I fed you, and not with meat, for ye were not yet able, but not even yet are ye now able,
texts.1co.3.3: for yet ye are fleshly, for where [there is] among you envying, and strife, and divisions, are ye not fleshly, and in the manner of men do walk?
texts.1co.3.4: for when one may say, `I, indeed, am of Paul;' and another, `I -- of Apollos;' are ye not fleshly?
texts.1co.3.5: Who, then, is Paul, and who Apollos, but ministrants through whom ye did believe, and to each as the Lord gave?
texts.1co.3.6: I planted, Apollos watered, but God was giving growth;
texts.1co.3.7: so that neither is he who is planting anything, nor he who is watering, but He who is giving growth -- God;
texts.1co.3.8: and he who is planting and he who is watering are one, and each his own reward shall receive, according to his own labour,
texts.1co.3.9: for of God we are fellow-workmen; God's tillage, God's building ye are.
texts.1co.3.10: According to the grace of God that was given to me, as a wise master-builder, a foundation I have laid, and another doth build on [it],
texts.1co.3.11: for other foundation no one is able to lay except that which is laid, which is Jesus the Christ;
texts.1co.3.12: and if any one doth build upon this foundation gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw --
texts.1co.3.13: of each the work shall become manifest, for the day shall declare [it], because in fire it is revealed, and the work of each, what kind it is, the fire shall prove;
texts.1co.3.14: if of any one the work doth remain that he built on [it], a wage he shall receive;
texts.1co.3.15: if of any the work is burned up, he shall suffer loss; and himself shall be saved, but so as through fire.
texts.1co.3.16: have ye not known that ye are a sanctuary of God, and the Spirit of God doth dwell in you?
texts.1co.3.17: if any one the sanctuary of God doth waste, him shall God waste; for the sanctuary of God is holy, the which ye are.
texts.1co.3.18: Let no one deceive himself; if any one doth seem to be wise among you in this age -- let him become a fool, that he may become wise,
texts.1co.3.19: for the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God, for it hath been written, `Who is taking the wise in their craftiness;'
texts.1co.3.20: and again, `The Lord doth know the reasonings of the wise, that they are vain.'
texts.1co.3.21: So then, let no one glory in men, for all things are yours,
texts.1co.3.22: whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things about to be -- all are yours,
texts.1co.3.23: and ye [are] Christ's, and Christ [is] God's.
texts.1co.4.1: Let a man so reckon us as officers of Christ, and stewards of the secrets of God,
texts.1co.4.2: and as to the rest, it is required in the stewards that one may be found faithful,
texts.1co.4.3: and to me it is for a very little thing that by you I may be judged, or by man's day, but not even myself do I judge,
texts.1co.4.4: for of nothing to myself have I been conscious, but not in this have I been declared right -- and he who is discerning me is the Lord:
texts.1co.4.5: so, then, nothing before the time judge ye, till the Lord may come, who will both bring to light the hidden things of the darkness, and will manifest the counsels of the hearts, and then the praise shall come to each from God.
texts.1co.4.6: And these things, brethren, I did transfer to myself and to Apollos because of you, that in us ye may learn not to think above that which hath been written, that ye may not be puffed up one for one against the other,
texts.1co.4.7: for who doth make thee to differ? and what hast thou, that thou didst not receive? and if thou didst also receive, why dost thou glory as not having received?
texts.1co.4.8: Already ye are having been filled, already ye were rich, apart from us ye did reign, and I would also ye did reign, that we also with you may reign together,
texts.1co.4.9: for I think that God did set forth us the apostles last -- as appointed to death, because a spectacle we became to the world, and messengers, and men;
texts.1co.4.10: we [are] fools because of Christ, and ye wise in Christ; we [are] ailing, and ye strong; ye glorious, and we dishonoured;
texts.1co.4.11: unto the present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and wander about,
texts.1co.4.12: and labour, working with [our] own hands; being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we suffer;
texts.1co.4.13: being spoken evil of, we entreat; as filth of the world we did become -- of all things an offscouring -- till now.
texts.1co.4.14: Not [as] putting you to shame do I write these things, but as my beloved children I do admonish,
texts.1co.4.15: for if a myriad of child-conductors ye may have in Christ, yet not many fathers; for in Christ Jesus, through the good news, I -- I did beget you;
texts.1co.4.16: I call upon you, therefore, become ye followers of me;
texts.1co.4.17: because of this I sent to you Timotheus, who is my child, beloved and faithful in the Lord, who shall remind you of my ways in Christ, according as everywhere in every assembly I teach.
texts.1co.4.18: And as if I were not coming unto you certain were puffed up;
texts.1co.4.19: but I will come quickly unto you, if the Lord may will, and I will know not the word of those puffed up, but the power;
texts.1co.4.20: for not in word is the reign of God, but in power?
texts.1co.4.21: what do ye wish? with a rod shall I come unto you, or in love, with a spirit also of meekness?
texts.1co.5.1: Whoredom is actually heard of among you, and such whoredom as is not even named among the nations -- as that one hath the wife of the father! --
texts.1co.5.2: and ye are having been puffed up, and did not rather mourn, that he may be removed out of the midst of you who did this work,
texts.1co.5.3: for I indeed, as being absent as to the body, and present as to the spirit, have already judged, as being present, him who so wrought this thing:
texts.1co.5.4: in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ -- ye being gathered together, also my spirit -- with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
texts.1co.5.5: to deliver up such a one to the Adversary for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
texts.1co.5.6: Not good [is] your glorying; have ye not known that a little leaven the whole lump doth leaven?
texts.1co.5.7: cleanse out, therefore, the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, according as ye are unleavened, for also our passover for us was sacrificed -- Christ,
texts.1co.5.8: so that we may keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of evil and wickedness, but with unleavened food of sincerity and truth.
texts.1co.5.9: I did write to you in the epistle, not to keep company with whoremongers --
texts.1co.5.10: and not certainly with the whoremongers of this world, or with the covetous, or extortioners, or idolaters, seeing ye ought then to go forth out of the world --
texts.1co.5.11: and now, I did write to you not to keep company with [him], if any one, being named a brother, may be a whoremonger, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner -- with such a one not even to eat together;
texts.1co.5.12: for what have I also those without to judge? those within do ye not judge?
texts.1co.5.13: and those without God doth judge; and put ye away the evil from among yourselves.
texts.1co.6.1: Dare any one of you, having a matter with the other, go to be judged before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?
texts.1co.6.2: have ye not known that the saints shall judge the world? and if by you the world is judged, are ye unworthy of the smaller judgments?
texts.1co.6.3: have ye not known that we shall judge messengers? why not then the things of life?
texts.1co.6.4: of the things of life, indeed, then, if ye may have judgment, those despised in the assembly -- these cause ye to sit;
texts.1co.6.5: unto your shame I speak: so there is not among you one wise man, not even one, who shall be able to discern in the midst of his brethren!
texts.1co.6.6: but brother with brother doth go to be judged, and this before unbelievers!
texts.1co.6.7: Already, indeed, then, there is altogether a fault among you, that ye have judgments with one another; wherefore do ye not rather suffer injustice? wherefore be ye not rather defrauded?
texts.1co.6.8: but ye -- ye do injustice, and ye defraud, and these -- brethren!
texts.1co.6.9: have ye not known that the unrighteous the reign of God shall not inherit? be not led astray; neither whoremongers, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor sodomites,
texts.1co.6.10: nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners, the reign of God shall inherit.
texts.1co.6.11: And certain of you were these! but ye were washed, but ye were sanctified, but ye were declared righteous, in the name of the Lord Jesus, and in the Spirit of our God.
texts.1co.6.12: All things are lawful to me, but all things are not profitable; all things are lawful to me, but I -- I will not be under authority by any;
texts.1co.6.13: the meats [are] for the belly, and the belly for the meats. And God both this and these shall make useless; and the body [is] not for whoredom, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body;
texts.1co.6.14: and God both the Lord did raise, and us will raise up through His power.
texts.1co.6.15: Have ye not known that your bodies are members of Christ? having taken, then, the members of the Christ, shall I make [them] members of an harlot? let it be not!
texts.1co.6.16: have ye not known that he who is joined to the harlot is one body? `for they shall be -- saith He -- the two for one flesh.'
texts.1co.6.17: And he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit;
texts.1co.6.18: flee the whoredom; every sin -- whatever a man may commit -- is without the body, and he who is committing whoredom, against his own body doth sin.
texts.1co.6.19: Have ye not known that your body is a sanctuary of the Holy Spirit in you, which ye have from God? and ye are not your own,
texts.1co.6.20: for ye were bought with a price; glorify, then, God in your body and in your spirit, which are God's.
texts.1co.7.1: And concerning the things of which ye wrote to me: good [it is] for a man not to touch a woman,
texts.1co.7.2: and because of the whoredom let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her proper husband;
texts.1co.7.3: to the wife let the husband the due benevolence render, and in like manner also the wife to the husband;
texts.1co.7.4: the wife over her own body hath not authority, but the husband; and, in like manner also, the husband over his own body hath not authority, but the wife.
texts.1co.7.5: Defraud not one another, except by consent for a time, that ye may be free for fasting and prayer, and again may come together, that the Adversary may not tempt you because of your incontinence;
texts.1co.7.6: and this I say by way of concurrence -- not of command,
texts.1co.7.7: for I wish all men to be even as I myself [am]; but each his own gift hath of God, one indeed thus, and one thus.
texts.1co.7.8: And I say to the unmarried and to the widows: it is good for them if they may remain even as I [am];
texts.1co.7.9: and if they have not continence -- let them marry, for it is better to marry than to burn;
texts.1co.7.10: and to the married I announce -- not I, but the Lord -- let not a wife separate from a husband:
texts.1co.7.11: but and if she may separate, let her remain unmarried, or to the husband let her be reconciled, and let not a husband send away a wife.
texts.1co.7.12: And to the rest I speak -- not the Lord -- if any brother hath a wife unbelieving, and she is pleased to dwell with him, let him not send her away;
texts.1co.7.13: and a woman who hath a husband unbelieving, and he is pleased to dwell with her, let her not send him away;
texts.1co.7.14: for the unbelieving husband hath been sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife hath been sanctified in the husband; otherwise your children are unclean, but now they are holy.
texts.1co.7.15: And, if the unbelieving doth separate himself -- let him separate himself: the brother or the sister is not under servitude in such [cases], and in peace hath God called us;
texts.1co.7.16: for what, hast thou known, O wife, whether the husband thou shalt save? or what, hast thou known, O husband, whether the wife thou shalt save?
texts.1co.7.17: if not, as God did distribute to each, as the Lord hath called each -- so let him walk; and thus in all the assemblies do I direct:
texts.1co.7.18: being circumcised -- was any one called? let him not become uncircumcised; in uncircumcision was any one called? let him not be circumcised;
texts.1co.7.19: the circumcision is nothing, and the uncircumcision is nothing -- but a keeping of the commands of God.
texts.1co.7.20: Each in the calling in which he was called -- in this let him remain;
texts.1co.7.21: a servant -- wast thou called? be not anxious; but if also thou art able to become free -- use [it] rather;
texts.1co.7.22: for he who [is] in the Lord -- having been called a servant -- is the Lord's freedman: in like manner also he the freeman, having been called, is servant of Christ:
texts.1co.7.23: with a price ye were bought, become not servants of men;
texts.1co.7.24: each, in that in which he was called, brethren, in this let him remain with God.
texts.1co.7.25: And concerning the virgins, a command of the Lord I have not; and I give judgment as having obtained kindness from the Lord to be faithful:
texts.1co.7.26: I suppose, therefore, this to be good because of the present necessity, that [it is] good for a man that the matter be thus: --
texts.1co.7.27: Hast thou been bound to a wife? seek not to be loosed; hast thou been loosed from a wife? seek not a wife.
texts.1co.7.28: But and if thou mayest marry, thou didst not sin; and if the virgin may marry, she did not sin; and such shall have tribulation in the flesh: and I spare you.
texts.1co.7.29: And this I say, brethren, the time henceforth is having been shortened -- that both those having wives may be as not having;
texts.1co.7.30: and those weeping, as not weeping; and those rejoicing, as not rejoicing; and those buying, as not possessing;
texts.1co.7.31: and those using this world, as not using [it] up; for passing away is the fashion of this world.
texts.1co.7.32: And I wish you to be without anxiety; the unmarried is anxious for the things of the Lord, how he shall please the Lord;
texts.1co.7.33: and the married is anxious for the things of the world, how he shall please the wife.
texts.1co.7.34: The wife and the virgin have been distinguished: the unmarried is anxious for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit, and the married is anxious for the things of the world, how she shall please the husband.
texts.1co.7.35: And this for your own profit I say: not that I may cast a noose upon you, but for the seemliness and devotedness to the Lord, undistractedly,
texts.1co.7.36: and if any one doth think [it] to be unseemly to his virgin, if she may be beyond the bloom of age, and it ought so to be, what he willeth let him do; he doth not sin -- let him marry.
texts.1co.7.37: And he who hath stood stedfast in the heart -- not having necessity -- and hath authority over his own will, and this he hath determined in his heart -- to keep his own virgin -- doth well;
texts.1co.7.38: so that both he who is giving in marriage doth well, and he who is not giving in marriage doth better.
texts.1co.7.39: A wife hath been bound by law as long time as her husband may live, and if her husband may sleep, she is free to be married to whom she will -- only in the Lord;
texts.1co.7.40: and she is happier if she may so remain -- according to my judgment; and I think I also have the Spirit of God.
texts.1co.8.1: And concerning the things sacrificed to idols, we have known that we all have knowledge: knowledge puffeth up, but love buildeth up;
texts.1co.8.2: and if any one doth think to know anything, he hath not yet known anything according as it behoveth [him] to know;
texts.1co.8.3: and if any one doth love God, this one hath been known by Him.
texts.1co.8.4: Concerning the eating then of the things sacrificed to idols, we have known that an idol [is] nothing in the world, and that there is no other God except one;
texts.1co.8.5: for even if there are those called gods, whether in heaven, whether upon earth -- as there are gods many and lords many --
texts.1co.8.6: yet to us [is] one God, the Father, of whom [are] the all things, and we to Him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom [are] the all things, and we through Him;
texts.1co.8.7: but not in all men [is] the knowledge, and certain with conscience of the idol, till now, as a thing sacrificed to an idol do eat [it], and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
texts.1co.8.8: But victuals do not commend us to God, for neither if we may eat are we in advance; nor if we may not eat, are we behind;
texts.1co.8.9: but see, lest this privilege of yours may become a stumbling-block to the infirm,
texts.1co.8.10: for if any one may see thee that hast knowledge in an idol's temple reclining at meat -- shall not his conscience -- he being infirm -- be emboldened to eat the things sacrificed to idols,
texts.1co.8.11: and the brother who is infirm shall perish by thy knowledge, because of whom Christ died?
texts.1co.8.12: and thus sinning in regard to the brethren, and smiting their weak conscience -- in regard to Christ ye sin;
texts.1co.8.13: wherefore, if victuals cause my brother to stumble, I may eat no flesh -- to the age -- that my brother I may not cause to stumble.
texts.1co.9.1: Am not I an apostle? am not I free? Jesus Christ our Lord have I not seen? my work are not ye in the Lord?
texts.1co.9.2: if to others I am not an apostle -- yet doubtless to you I am; for the seal of my apostleship are ye in the Lord.
texts.1co.9.3: My defence to those who examine me in this;
texts.1co.9.4: have we not authority to eat and to drink?
texts.1co.9.5: have we not authority a sister -- a wife -- to lead about, as also the other apostles, and the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas?
texts.1co.9.6: or only I and Barnabas, have we not authority -- not to work?
texts.1co.9.7: who doth serve as a soldier at his own charges at any time? who doth plant a vineyard, and of its fruit doth not eat? or who doth feed a flock, and of the milk of the flock doth not eat?
texts.1co.9.8: According to man do I speak these things? or doth not also the law say these things?
texts.1co.9.9: for in the law of Moses it hath been written, `thou shalt not muzzle an ox treading out corn;' for the oxen doth God care?
texts.1co.9.10: or because of us by all means doth He say [it]? yes, because of us it was written, because in hope ought the plower to plow, and he who is treading [ought] of his hope to partake in hope.
texts.1co.9.11: If we to you the spiritual things did sow -- great [is it] if we your fleshly things do reap?
texts.1co.9.12: if others do partake of the authority over you -- not we more? but we did not use this authority, but all things we bear, that we may give no hindrance to the good news of the Christ.
texts.1co.9.13: Have ye not known that those working about the things of the temple -- of the temple do eat, and those waiting at the altar -- with the altar are partakers?
texts.1co.9.14: so also did the Lord direct to those proclaiming the good news: of the good news to live.
texts.1co.9.15: And I have used none of these things; neither did I write these things that it may be so done in my case, for [it is] good for me rather to die, than that any one may make my glorying void;
texts.1co.9.16: for if I may proclaim good news, it is no glorying for me, for necessity is laid upon me, and wo is to me if I may not proclaim good news;
texts.1co.9.17: for if willing I do this, I have a reward; and if unwillingly -- with a stewardship I have been entrusted!
texts.1co.9.18: What, then, is my reward? -- that proclaiming good news, without charge I shall make the good news of the Christ, not to abuse my authority in the good news;
texts.1co.9.19: for being free from all men, to all men I made myself servant, that the more I might gain;
texts.1co.9.20: and I became to the Jews as a Jew, that Jews I might gain; to those under law as under law, that those under law I might gain;
texts.1co.9.21: to those without law, as without law -- (not being without law to God, but within law to Christ) -- that I might gain those without law;
texts.1co.9.22: I became to the infirm as infirm, that the infirm I might gain; to all men I have become all things, that by all means I may save some.
texts.1co.9.23: And this I do because of the good news, that a fellow-partaker of it I may become;
texts.1co.9.24: have ye not known that those running in a race -- all indeed run, but one doth receive the prize? so run ye, that ye may obtain;
texts.1co.9.25: and every one who is striving, is in all things temperate; these, indeed, then, that a corruptible crown they may receive, but we an incorruptible;
texts.1co.9.26: I, therefore, thus run, not as uncertainly, thus I fight, as not beating air;
texts.1co.9.27: but I chastise my body, and bring [it] into servitude, lest by any means, having preached to others -- I myself may become disapproved.
texts.1co.10.1: And I do not wish you to be ignorant, brethren, that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea,
texts.1co.10.2: and all to Moses were baptized in the cloud, and in the sea;
texts.1co.10.3: and all the same spiritual food did eat,
texts.1co.10.4: and all the same spiritual drink did drink, for they were drinking of a spiritual rock following them, and the rock was the Christ;
texts.1co.10.5: but in the most of them God was not well pleased, for they were strewn in the wilderness,
texts.1co.10.6: and those things became types of us, for our not passionately desiring evil things, as also these did desire.
texts.1co.10.7: Neither become ye idolaters, as certain of them, as it hath been written, `The people sat down to eat and to drink, and stood up to play;'
texts.1co.10.8: neither may we commit whoredom, as certain of them did commit whoredom, and there fell in one day twenty-three thousand;
texts.1co.10.9: neither may we tempt the Christ, as also certain of them did tempt, and by the serpents did perish;
texts.1co.10.10: neither murmur ye, as also some of them did murmur, and did perish by the destroyer.
texts.1co.10.11: And all these things as types did happen to those persons, and they were written for our admonition, to whom the end of the ages did come,
texts.1co.10.12: so that he who is thinking to stand -- let him observe, lest he fall.
texts.1co.10.13: No temptation hath taken you -- except human; and God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above what ye are able, but He will make, with the temptation, also the outlet, for your being able to bear [it].
texts.1co.10.14: Wherefore, my beloved, flee from the idolatry;
texts.1co.10.15: as to wise men I speak -- judge ye what I say:
texts.1co.10.16: The cup of the blessing that we bless -- is it not the fellowship of the blood of the Christ? the bread that we break -- is it not the fellowship of the body of the Christ?
texts.1co.10.17: because one bread, one body, are we the many -- for we all of the one bread do partake.
texts.1co.10.18: See Israel according to the flesh! are not those eating the sacrifices in the fellowship of the altar?
texts.1co.10.19: what then do I say? that an idol is anything? or that a sacrifice offered to an idol is anything? --
texts.1co.10.20: [no,] but that the things that the nations sacrifice -- they sacrifice to demons and not to God; and I do not wish you to come into the fellowship of the demons.
texts.1co.10.21: Ye are not able the cup of the Lord to drink, and the cup of demons; ye are not able of the table of the Lord to partake, and of the table of demons;
texts.1co.10.22: do we arouse the Lord to jealousy? are we stronger than He?
texts.1co.10.23: All things to me are lawful, but all things are not profitable; all things to me are lawful, but all things do not build up;
texts.1co.10.24: let no one seek his own -- but each another's.
texts.1co.10.25: Whatever in the meat-market is sold eat ye, not inquiring, because of the conscience,
texts.1co.10.26: for the Lord's [is] the earth, and its fulness;
texts.1co.10.27: and if any one of the unbelieving do call you, and ye wish to go, all that is set before you eat, nothing inquiring, because of the conscience;
texts.1co.10.28: and if any one may say to you, `This is a thing sacrificed to an idol,' -- do not eat, because of that one who shewed [it], and of the conscience, for the Lord's [is] the earth and its fulness:
texts.1co.10.29: and conscience, I say, not of thyself, but of the other, for why [is it] that my liberty is judged by another's conscience?
texts.1co.10.30: and if I thankfully do partake, why am I evil spoken of, for that for which I give thanks?
texts.1co.10.31: Whether, then, ye eat, or drink, or do anything, do all to the glory of God;
texts.1co.10.32: become offenceless, both to Jews and Greeks, and to the assembly of God;
texts.1co.10.33: as I also in all things do please all, not seeking my own profit, but that of many -- that they may be saved.
texts.1co.11.1: Followers of me become ye, as I also [am] of Christ.
texts.1co.11.2: And I praise you, brethren, that in all things ye remember me, and according as I did deliver to you, the deliverances ye keep,
texts.1co.11.3: and I wish you to know that of every man the head is the Christ, and the head of a woman is the husband, and the head of Christ is God.
texts.1co.11.4: Every man praying or prophesying, having the head covered, doth dishonour his head,
texts.1co.11.5: and every woman praying or prophesying with the head uncovered, doth dishonour her own head, for it is one and the same thing with her being shaven,
texts.1co.11.6: for if a woman is not covered -- then let her be shorn, and if [it is] a shame for a woman to be shorn or shaven -- let her be covered;
texts.1co.11.7: for a man, indeed, ought not to cover the head, being the image and glory of God, and a woman is the glory of a man,
texts.1co.11.8: for a man is not of a woman, but a woman [is] of a man,
texts.1co.11.9: for a man also was not created because of the woman, but a woman because of the man;
texts.1co.11.10: because of this the woman ought to have [a token of] authority upon the head, because of the messengers;
texts.1co.11.11: but neither [is] a man apart from a woman, nor a woman apart from a man, in the Lord,
texts.1co.11.12: for as the woman [is] of the man, so also the man [is] through the woman, and the all things [are] of God.
texts.1co.11.13: In your own selves judge ye; is it seemly for a woman uncovered to pray to God?
texts.1co.11.14: doth not even nature itself teach you, that if a man indeed have long hair, a dishonour it is to him?
texts.1co.11.15: and a woman, if she have long hair, a glory it is to her, because the hair instead of a covering hath been given to her;
texts.1co.11.16: and if any one doth think to be contentious, we have no such custom, neither the assemblies of God.
texts.1co.11.17: And this declaring, I give no praise, because not for the better, but for the worse ye come together;
texts.1co.11.18: for first, indeed, ye coming together in an assembly, I hear of divisions being among you, and partly I believe [it],
texts.1co.11.19: for it behoveth sects also to be among you, that those approved may become manifest among you;
texts.1co.11.20: ye, then, coming together at the same place -- it is not to eat the Lord's supper;
texts.1co.11.21: for each his own supper doth take before in the eating, and one is hungry, and another is drunk;
texts.1co.11.22: why, have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? or the assembly of God do ye despise, and shame those not having? what may I say to you? shall I praise you in this? I do not praise!
texts.1co.11.23: For I -- I received from the Lord that which also I did deliver to you, that the Lord Jesus in the night in which he was delivered up, took bread,
texts.1co.11.24: and having given thanks, he brake, and said, `Take ye, eat ye, this is my body, that for you is being broken; this do ye -- to the remembrance of me.'
texts.1co.11.25: In like manner also the cup after the supping, saying, `This cup is the new covenant in my blood; this do ye, as often as ye may drink [it] -- to the remembrance of me;'
texts.1co.11.26: for as often as ye may eat this bread, and this cup may drink, the death of the Lord ye do shew forth -- till he may come;
texts.1co.11.27: so that whoever may eat this bread or may drink the cup of the Lord unworthily, guilty he shall be of the body and blood of the Lord:
texts.1co.11.28: and let a man be proving himself, and so of the bread let him eat, and of the cup let him drink;
texts.1co.11.29: for he who is eating and drinking unworthily, judgment to himself he doth eat and drink -- not discerning the body of the Lord.
texts.1co.11.30: Because of this, among you many [are] weak and sickly, and sleep do many;
texts.1co.11.31: for if ourselves we were discerning, we would not be being judged,
texts.1co.11.32: and being judged by the Lord, we are chastened, that with the world we may not be condemned;
texts.1co.11.33: so then, my brethren, coming together to eat, for one another wait ye;
texts.1co.11.34: and if any one is hungry, at home let him eat, that to judgment ye may not come together; and the rest, whenever I may come, I shall arrange.
texts.1co.12.1: And concerning the spiritual things, brethren, I do not wish you to be ignorant;
texts.1co.12.2: ye have known that ye were nations, unto the dumb idols -- as ye were led -- being carried away;
texts.1co.12.3: wherefore, I give you to understand that no one, in the Spirit of God speaking, saith Jesus [is] anathema, and no one is able to say Jesus [is] Lord, except in the Holy Spirit.
