texts.1co.1.26: For be looking at the calling of you, brethren,—that [there were] not many wise, according to flesh. Not many powerful, not many high-born:
texts.1co.1.27: On the contrary—the foolish things of the world, hath God chosen, that he might put to shame them who are wise, and, the weak things of the world, hath God chosen, that he might put to shame the things that are mighty,
texts.1co.1.28: And, the low-born things of the world, and the things that are despised, hath God chosen,— [and] the things that are not,—that, the things that are, he might bring to nought;
texts.1co.1.29: So that no flesh should boast before God.
texts.1co.1.30: But, of him, are, ye, in Christ Jesus, who hath been made wisdom unto us, from God,—both righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption:
texts.1co.1.31: In order that, even as it is written—He that boasteth, in the Lord, let him boast.
texts.1co.2.1: I, therefore, brethren, when I came unto you, came, not with excellency of discourse or wisdom, declaring unto you the mystery of God;
texts.1co.2.2: For I had not determined to know anything among you, save Jesus Christ,—and, him, as one who had been crucified!
texts.1co.2.3: I, therefore in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling, came to be with you,
texts.1co.2.4: And, my discourse, and what I proclaimed, were not in suasive words of wisdom, but in demonstration of Spirit and power:
texts.1co.2.5: In order that, your faith, might not be in men’s wisdom, but in God’s power.
texts.1co.2.6: Wisdom, however, we do speak, among the full-grown,—wisdom, indeed, not of this age, nor of the rulers of this age, who are to come to nought;
texts.1co.2.7: But we speak, God’s, wisdom, in a sacred secret, that hidden [wisdom], which God marked out beforehand, before the ages, for our glory,—
texts.1co.2.8: Which, none of the rulers of this age had come to know, for, had they known, not, in that case, the Lord of the glory, would they have crucified!
texts.1co.2.9: But, even as it is written—The things which eye hath not seen, and ear hath not heard, and upon the heart of man have not come up,—whatsoever things God hath prepared for them that love him,
texts.1co.2.10: Unto us, in fact, hath God revealed through the Spirit; for, the Spirit, into all things, maketh search, yea! the deep things of God.
texts.1co.2.11: For who of men knoweth the things of a man,—save the spirit of the man that is in him? thus, even the things of God, hath no one come to know, save the Spirit of God.
texts.1co.2.12: But, as for us,—not the spirit of the world, have we received, but the Spirit which is of God,—that we might know the things which, by God, have been given in favour unto us:—
texts.1co.2.13: Which we also speak—not in words taught of human wisdom, but in such as are taught of [the] Spirit, by spiritual words, spiritual things, explaining.
texts.1co.2.14: But, a man of the soul, doth not welcome the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness unto him, and he cannot get to know them, because, spiritually, are they examined;
texts.1co.2.15: But, the man of the spirit, on the one hand, examineth all things, but, on the other, he himself, by no one, is examined.
texts.1co.2.16: For who hath come to know the mind of the Lord, that shall instruct him? But, we, have, the mind of Christ.
texts.1co.3.1: I, therefore, brethren, have not been able to speak unto you, as unto men of the Spirit, but as unto men of the flesh—as unto babes in Christ:—
texts.1co.3.2: With milk, have I fed you, not, with meat; for, not yet, have ye been able;—nay! not [yet] even now, are ye able,
texts.1co.3.3: For ye are yet fleshly. For, whereas there are, among you, jealousy and strife, are ye not, fleshly, and, after the manner of men, walking?
texts.1co.3.4: For, as soon as one beginneth to say—I, indeed, am of Paul! and another—I, of Apollos! are ye not, men?
texts.1co.3.5: What then is Apollos? and, what is Paul? ministers through whom ye believed, and, each, as the Lord, gave to him.
texts.1co.3.6: I, planted, Apollos, watered,—but, God, caused to, grow.
texts.1co.3.7: So that, [neither] is he that planteth anything, nor, he that watereth,—but, God, who causeth to, grow.
texts.1co.3.8: Moreover, he that planteth and he that watereth, are one:—howbeit, each one, his own reward, shall receive,—according to his own labour.
texts.1co.3.9: For we are, God’s, fellow-workmen: ye are, God’s, farm, God’s building.
texts.1co.3.10: According to the favour of God which hath been given unto me, as a wise master-builder, I laid a foundation, whereas, another, is building thereon; but, let each one, see, how he buildeth thereon;
texts.1co.3.11: For, other foundation, can, no one, lay, than that which is lying, which is, Jesus Christ.
texts.1co.3.12: But, if anyone is building, upon the foundation—gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw,
texts.1co.3.13: Each one’s work, shall be made, manifest; for, the day, will make it plain, because, by fire, is it to be revealed,—and, each one’s work, of what sort it is, the fire itself will prove:—
texts.1co.3.14: If, anyone’s work, shall abide, which he built, a reward, shall he receive,—
texts.1co.3.15: If, anyone’s work, shall be burnt up, he shall suffer loss, but shall, himself, be saved—though, thus, as through fire.
texts.1co.3.16: Know ye not that ye are a shrine of God, and that the Spirit of God within you doth dwell?
texts.1co.3.17: If anyone doth mar the shrine of God, God, will mar him; for the shrine of God is holy,—and such are ye.
texts.1co.3.18: Let no one be deceiving himself:—if anyone imagineth himself to be wise among you, in this age, let him become foolish, that he may become wise;
texts.1co.3.19: For, the wisdom of this world, is, foolishness with God; for it is written—He that taketh the wise in their knavery,—
texts.1co.3.20: And again—The Lord taketh note of the speculations of the wise, that they are vain.
texts.1co.3.21: So then, let, no one, be boasting in men; for, all things, are yours—
texts.1co.3.22: Whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come, all, are, yours,
texts.1co.3.23: And, ye, are Christ’s,—and, Christ, is, God’s.
texts.1co.4.1: Let a man, so, be reckoning of us, as officers of Christ, and stewards of sacred secrets of God.
texts.1co.4.2: Here, furthermore, it is sought in stewards, that, faithful, one be found.
texts.1co.4.3: With me, however, it counteth for the very smallest thing, that, by you, I should be examined, or by a human day. Nay! I am not even examining myself,
texts.1co.4.4: For, of nothing, to myself, am I conscious: nevertheless, not hereby, am I declared righteous, but, he that doth examine me, is the Lord.
texts.1co.4.5: So then, not before the fitting time, be judging anything,—until the Lord shall come, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and make manifest the counsels of the hearts; and, then, the praise shall come to each one, from God.
texts.1co.4.6: But, these things, brethren, have I transferred unto myself and Apollos, for your sakes, that, in us, ye might learn [the lesson] —Not beyond the things that are written…! that ye do not puff yourselves up, individually, for this one against that.
texts.1co.4.7: For who maketh thee to differ? and what hast thou which thou didst not receive? But, if thou didst even receive it, why dost thou boast, as though thou hadst not received it?
texts.1co.4.8: Already, ye have become full, already, ye are become rich,—apart from us, ye are become kings! And I would indeed ye had become kings, that, we also, with you, might have together become kings!
texts.1co.4.9: For I think that, God, hath set forth, us the apostles, to be last of all, as men devoted to death,—in that, a spectacle, have we been made, unto the world,—both unto messengers and unto men.
texts.1co.4.10: We, are foolish for Christ’s sake, but, ye, prudent in Christ; we are weak, but, ye, mighty; ye, all-glorious, but, we, dishonoured.
texts.1co.4.11: Until the present hour, we both hunger and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and are wanderers,
texts.1co.4.12: And toil, working with our own hands: being reviled, we bless, being persecuted, we hold on,
texts.1co.4.13: Being defamed, we beseech: as the sweepings of the world have we become, the offscouring of all—until even now.
texts.1co.4.14: Not, to shame you, write I these things; but, as my beloved children, I admonish you.
texts.1co.4.15: For, though myriads of tutors ye should have in Christ, yet not many fathers; for, in Christ Jesus, through means of the joyful message, I, begat you.
texts.1co.4.16: I beseech you, therefore,—become imitators of me.
texts.1co.4.17: For this cause, sent I unto you, Timothy,—who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who shall put, you, in mind of my ways which are in Christ [Jesus], even as, everywhere, in every assembly, I teach.
texts.1co.4.18: But, as though I were not coming unto you, some are puffed up!
texts.1co.4.19: Howbeit, I will come quickly unto you,—if, the Lord, please,—and will get to know—not the speech of them who are puffed up, but, the power;
texts.1co.4.20: For, not in speech, is the kingdom of God, but, in power.
texts.1co.4.21: What will ye? that, with a rod, I should come unto you? or, with love, and a spirit of meekness?
texts.1co.5.1: On all hands, there is reported to be among you—fornication, and such fornication as this—which, not among the nations, [is found],—as that one should have, his father’s wife:—
texts.1co.5.2: And, ye, have become puffed up, and have not rather mourned, in order that he might be removed out of your midst, who, this deed, hath wrought.
texts.1co.5.3: For, I, indeed,—being absent in the body, but present in the spirit, have already judged, as present, him who, thus, this thing hath perpetrated:—
texts.1co.5.4: In the name of our Lord Jesus, ye being gathered together, and my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus,
texts.1co.5.5: To deliver such a one as this, unto Satan, for the destruction of the flesh,—that, the spirit, may be saved in the day of the Lord.
texts.1co.5.6: Unseemly, is your boast! Know ye not that, a little leaven, doth leaven, the whole of the lump?
texts.1co.5.7: Purge ye out the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump,—even as ye are unleavened; for, our passover, hath even been sacrificed—Christ:
texts.1co.5.8: So then, let us be keeping the feast, not with old leaven, nor with leaven of baseness and wickedness,—but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
texts.1co.5.9: I wrote unto you in my letter—not to be mixing yourselves up with fornicators;—
texts.1co.5.10: Not at all, [meaning] the fornicators of this world, or the covetous and extortioners, or idolaters,—else had ye been obliged, in that case, to go out of the world!
texts.1co.5.11: But, now, I have written unto you not to be mixing yourselves up,—if anyone named a brother, be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or an extortioner, with such a one as this, not so much, as to be eating together,
texts.1co.5.12: For what have I to do to be judging them who are without? Do, ye, not judge, them who are within,
texts.1co.5.13: Whereas, them who are without, God, judgeth? Remove ye the wicked man from among, yourselves.
texts.1co.6.1: Dare any of you, having, a matter against his brother, sue for judgment before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?
texts.1co.6.2: Or know ye not that, the saints, shall judge the world? And, if, by you, the world, is to be judged, unworthy are ye of the smallest judgment-seats?
texts.1co.6.3: Know ye not that we shall judge, messengers? and not, then, matters of this life?
texts.1co.6.4: If, then, for matters of this, life ye have judgment-seats, them who are of no account in the assembly, these, are ye seating thereupon?
texts.1co.6.5: With a view to shame you, am I speaking. So, is it possible that there is among you—not so much as one wise man, who shall be able to judge between his brethren,—
texts.1co.6.6: But, brother with brother, sueth for judgment, and that before unbelievers?
texts.1co.6.7: Already, indeed, it is an utter defeat for you, that ye are having, law-suits, one with another. Wherefore are ye not rather taking wrong? Wherefore are ye not rather suffering yourselves to be defrauded?
texts.1co.6.8: Nay! but, ye, are doing wrong, and defrauding,—and that [your] brethren.
texts.1co.6.9: Or know ye not that, wrong-doers, shall not inherit, God’s kingdom? Be not deceiving yourselves:—neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor sodomites,
texts.1co.6.10: Nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners—shall inherit, God’s kingdom.
texts.1co.6.11: And, these things, were some of you; but ye bathed them away,—but ye were sanctified, but ye were justified, in the name of [our] Lord Jesus Christ, and in the Spirit of our God.
texts.1co.6.12: All things, unto me, are allowable, but, not all things, are profitable: all things, unto me, are allowable, but, I, will not be brought under authority by any.
texts.1co.6.13: Foods for the belly, and the belly for foods; but, God, will set aside, both it and them. The body, however, is not for fornication, but, for the Lord,—and, the Lord, for the body.
texts.1co.6.14: God, moreover, hath both raised up, the Lord, and will raise, us, up from among [the dead] through his power.
texts.1co.6.15: Know ye not that, your bodies, are, members of Christ? Shall I, then, take away the members of the Christ and make them members of a harlot? Far be it!
texts.1co.6.16: Or know ye not that, he that joineth himself unto the harlot, is, one body? For, saith he, the two, shall become, one flesh;
texts.1co.6.17: But, he that joineth himself unto the Lord, is, one Spirit.
texts.1co.6.18: Flee fornication! Every sin, whatsoever a man shall commit, is, outside his body, but, he that committeth fornication, bringeth sin into his own body.
texts.1co.6.19: Or know ye not that, your body, is, a shrine of the Holy Spirit that is within you, which ye have from God? And ye are not your own;—
texts.1co.6.20: For ye have been bought with a price! Therefore glorify God in your body.
texts.1co.7.1: Now, concerning the things whereof ye wrote, it were, good, for a man, not to touch, a woman;
texts.1co.7.2: But, on account of fornications, let, each man, have, his own wife, and, each woman, have, her own husband:
texts.1co.7.3: Unto the wife, let the husband render what is her due, and, in like manner, the wife also, unto the husband,—
texts.1co.7.4: The wife, over her own body, hath not authority, but the husband, and, in like manner, the husband also, over his own body, hath not authority, but the wife.
texts.1co.7.5: Be not depriving one another—unless perhaps by consent for a season, that ye may have leisure for prayer, and, again, may be together,—lest Satan be tempting you by reason of your want of self-control.
texts.1co.7.6: This, however I am saying, by way of concession, not of injunction;
texts.1co.7.7: Besides, I desire all men to be, even as myself,—but, each one, hath his, personal, gift from God, one, after this manner, and, another, after that.
texts.1co.7.8: But I say, to the unmarried, and to the widows, good, were it for them, that they should abide, even as I;
texts.1co.7.9: But, if they have not self-control, let them marry, for, better, is it, to marry than to burn.
texts.1co.7.10: To the married, however, I give charge—not, I, but the Lord,—that, a wife, from her husband, do not depart,—
texts.1co.7.11: But, if she should even depart, let her remain unmarried, or, to her husband, be reconciled; and let not, a husband, leave, his wife.
texts.1co.7.12: But, unto the rest, say, I—not the Lord,—if, any brother, hath, a wife that believeth not, and, she, is well pleased to dwell with him, let him not leave her;
texts.1co.7.13: And, a woman who hath a husband that believeth not, and, he, is well pleased to dwell with her, let her not leave her husband;—
texts.1co.7.14: For the husband that believeth not is hallowed in the wife, and the wife that believeth not is hallowed in the brother: else were, your children, impure, but, now, are they, pure.
texts.1co.7.15: But, if, the unbelieving, departeth, let him depart: the brother or the sister hath not come into bondage, in such cases, but, in peace, hath God called us.
texts.1co.7.16: For how knowest thou, O woman, whether, thy husband, thou shalt save? Or how knowest thou, O man, whether, thy wife, thou shalt save?
texts.1co.7.17: If not—as the Lord hath distributed—unto each one, as God hath called, each one, so, let him be walking;—and, so, in all the assemblies, I ordain.
texts.1co.7.18: After being circumcised, was any called? let him not become uncircumcised; in uncircumcision, hath any been called? let him not be circumcised:
texts.1co.7.19: The circumcision, is, nothing, and, the uncircumcision, is, nothing,—but keeping the commandments of God.
texts.1co.7.20: Each one, in the calling wherein he was called, in the same, let him abide:
texts.1co.7.21: A bond-servant, wast thou called? let it not cause thee concern; but, if thou canst even become, free, rather use it.
texts.1co.7.22: For, he who in the Lord was called, being a bond-servant, is, a freed-man of the Lord: in like manner, he that was called being, a freeman, is Christ’s bond-servant:—
texts.1co.7.23: With a price, have ye been bought,—do not become bond-servants of men:
texts.1co.7.24: Each one, wherein he was called, brethren, in the same, let him abide with God.
texts.1co.7.25: But, concerning them who are virgin, injunction of the Lord, have I none; yet, a judgment, do I give, as one who hath obtained mercy from the Lord to be, faithful:
texts.1co.7.26: I consider this, then, to be, good, in the circumstances, by reason of the existing distress,—that it is, good for a man, so, to be:
texts.1co.7.27: Hast thou become bound to a wife? do not seek to be loosed; hast thou become loosed from a wife? do not seek a wife.
texts.1co.7.28: If, however, thou shouldst even marry, thou hast not sinned; and, if one who is virgin should marry, that one hath not sinned;—but, tribulation of the flesh, shall, such, have:—howbeit, I, spare you.
texts.1co.7.29: But, this, I say—the opportunity is, contracted for what remaineth—in order that, they who have wives, may be, as though they had none,
texts.1co.7.30: And, they who weep, as though they wept not, and, they who rejoice, as though they rejoiced not, and, they who buy, as though they possessed not,
texts.1co.7.31: And, they who use the world, as though they used it not to the full,—for the fashion of this world passeth away;
texts.1co.7.32: And I desire you to be, without anxiety:—the unmarried man, is anxious for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;
texts.1co.7.33: But, he that hath married, is anxious for the things of the world, how may please his wife—
texts.1co.7.34: And he is divided; and, the unmarried woman, or the virgin, is anxious for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy [both] in her body and in her spirit; but, she that hath married, is anxious for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.
texts.1co.7.35: This, however, with a view to your own profit, am I saying,—not that, a snare, upon you, I may cast, but with a view to what is comely, and devoted unto the Lord, without distraction.
texts.1co.7.36: If however anyone considereth it behaving unseemly towards his virginity, if he should be beyond the bloom of life,—and, thus, it ought to come about, what he chooseth, let him do,—he sinneth not: let them marry:
texts.1co.7.37: But, he that standeth in his heart, steadfast, having no necessity, but hath authority concerning his own will, and, this, hath determined in his own heart,—to preserve his own virginity, well shall he do.
texts.1co.7.38: So that, he that giveth in marriage his own virginity, doeth, well; and, he that giveth it not, shall do, better.
texts.1co.7.39: A wife, is bound for as long a time as her husband is living; but, if the husband have fallen asleep, she is, free, to be married unto whom she pleaseth,—only, in the Lord;
texts.1co.7.40: But, happier, is she, if, so, she remain,—in my judgment; for I think, I also, have the Spirit of God.
texts.1co.8.1: Now, concerning the idol-sacrifices, we are aware—because we, all, have knowledge,—knowledge, puffeth up, but, love, buildeth up;
texts.1co.8.2: If anyone thinketh that he knoweth anything, not yet knoweth he, as he must needs come to know,
texts.1co.8.3: But, if anyone loveth God, the same, is known of him—
texts.1co.8.4: Concerning, then, the eating of idol-sacrifices, we are aware—that an idol is, nothing, in the world, and that, none, is God save one.
texts.1co.8.5: For, if indeed there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or upon earth,—as indeed there are gods many and lords many,
texts.1co.8.6: [Yet], to us, there is one God the Father, of whom are all things, and, we, for him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and, we, through him.
texts.1co.8.7: Howbeit, not in all, is the knowledge; but, some, by their familiarity, until even now, with the idol, as an idol-sacrifice, eat it, and, their conscience, being, weak, is defiled.
texts.1co.8.8: Food, indeed, will not commend us unto God,—neither, if we eat not, do we lack, nor, if we eat, do we abound.
texts.1co.8.9: But be taking heed, lest, by any means, your right, itself, become, an occasion of stumbling, unto the weak;
texts.1co.8.10: For, if anyone should see [thee] who hast knowledge, in an idol-temple, reclining, will not, his conscience, being, weak, be built up for the eating of the idol-sacrifices?
texts.1co.8.11: In fact, he that is weak, is being destroyed, by thy knowledge—the brother for whose sake Christ died.
texts.1co.8.12: But, in thus sinning against the brethren am wounding their conscience, seeing it is weak, against Christ, are ye sinning.
texts.1co.8.13: Therefore, if food is an occasion of stumbling unto my brother, in nowise will I eat flesh unto the age that abideth,—that, I may not occasion, my brother, to stumble.
texts.1co.9.1: Am not free? Am I not an apostle? Jesus our Lord, have I not seen? Are not, ye, my work, in the Lord?
texts.1co.9.2: If, unto others, I am not an apostle, certainly at least, unto you, I am; for, the seal of my apostleship, ye, are in the Lord.
texts.1co.9.3: My defence, unto them who are examining me, is this:
texts.1co.9.4: Have we not a right to eat and drink?
texts.1co.9.5: Have we not a right to take round, a sister wife,—as even the rest of the apostles, and the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas?
texts.1co.9.6: Or have, only I and Barnabas, not a right to forbear working?
texts.1co.9.7: Who serveth as a soldier, at his own charges, at any time? Who planteth a vineyard,—and, the fruit thereof, doth not eat? [Or] who shepherdeth a flock,—and, of the milk of the flock, doth not eat?
texts.1co.9.8: Is it, after the manner of men, that these things I am saying? Or doth not, even the law, the same things, say?
texts.1co.9.9: For, in the law of Moses, it is written—Thou shalt not muzzle an ox when it is treading out the corn:—Is it, for the oxen, God is caring?
texts.1co.9.10: Or, for our sakes altogether, is he saying it? For our sakes, it was written; because, he that ploweth, ought, to plow, in hope,—and, he that thresheth, [to thresh] in hope of partaking.
texts.1co.9.11: If, we, unto you, the things of the Spirit have sown, is it a great matter, if, we, of you, the things of the flesh shall reap?
texts.1co.9.12: If, others, of this right, over you, are partaking, [should] not rather, we? nevertheless, we used not this right; but, all [such] things, do we conceal,—lest we should cause any hindrance unto the glad message of the Christ.
texts.1co.9.13: Know ye not that, they who labour in the holy rites, do eat the provisions out of the holy place? They who at the altar wait, do, with the altar, share?
texts.1co.9.14: Thus, also, hath the Lord, appointed—that, they who the glad message tell, should, of the glad-message, live.
texts.1co.9.15: I, however, have not used any of these things; and have not written these things, in order that, so it should be done, in my case; for it were, good for me, rather to die than——my boast, shall, no man, make void!
texts.1co.9.16: For, if I be telling the glad-message, it is, with me, no matter of boasting; for, necessity, upon me, lieth,—for it is, Woe to me, if I should not be telling the glad-message;
texts.1co.9.17: For, if, by choice, this thing I am doing, I have, a reward; but, if not by choice, with a stewardship, have I been entrusted!
texts.1co.9.18: What, then, is my reward? that, in telling the glad-message, free of cost, I should put the glad-message,—to the end I should not use to the full my right in the glad-message.
texts.1co.9.19: For, though free from all, unto all, myself, I enslaved,—that, the larger number, I might win:
texts.1co.9.20: Therefore became I, to the Jews, as, a Jew,—that, Jews, I might win; to them who were under law, as, under law, not being, myself, under law,—that, them who were under law, I might win;
texts.1co.9.21: To them who were without law, as, without law,—not being without law to God, but lawfully subject to Christ,—that I might win them who were without law.
texts.1co.9.22: I became, unto the weak, weak,—that, the weak, I might win;—to all men, have I become all things, that, by all means, some, I might save.
texts.1co.9.23: But, all things, am I doing, for the sake of the glad-message, that a joint-partaker thereof, I may become.
texts.1co.9.24: Know ye not that, they who, in a racecourse, run, all, indeed, run,—but, one, receiveth the prize? So, be running, that ye may lay hold.
texts.1co.9.25: But, every man who striveth in the games, in all things, useth self-control;—they, indeed, then, that a corruptible crown, they may receive; but, we, an incorruptible!
texts.1co.9.26: I, therefore, so, am running, as, not uncertainly, so, am boxing, as not thrashing air;
texts.1co.9.27: But am beating my body under, and leading it captive, lest, by any means,—unto others, having proclaimed, [the contest], I myself, should be rejected.
texts.1co.10.1: For I wish not ye should be ignorant, brethren, that, all our fathers, were, under the cloud, and, all, passed through the sea,—
texts.1co.10.2: And, all, immersed themselves into Moses, in the cloud, and in the sea;
texts.1co.10.3: And, all, did eat [the same] spiritual food,
texts.1co.10.4: And, all, drank, the same spiritual drink,—for they continued to drink of the spiritual rock that followed them, and, the rock, was the Christ:—
texts.1co.10.5: Nevertheless, with the most of them, God, was not well-pleased, for they were strewed along in the desert.
texts.1co.10.6: But, in these things, they became, ensamples for us, to the end we should not be covetous of evil things, even as, they, also coveted;
texts.1co.10.7: Neither become ye, idolaters, as some of them,—as it is written—The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to be making sport;
texts.1co.10.8: Neither let us commit fornication, as, some of them, committed fornication, and there fell, in one day, three and twenty thousand;
texts.1co.10.9: Neither let us be putting the Lord to the test, as, some of them, put him to the test, and, by the serpents, were perishing;
texts.1co.10.10: Neither be ye murmuring, even, as some of them, murmured, and perished by the destroyer.
texts.1co.10.11: But, these things, by way of type, were happening unto them, and were written with a view to our admonition, unto whom, the ends of the ages, have reached along.
texts.1co.10.12: So that, he that thinketh he is standing, let him take heed lest he fall.
texts.1co.10.13: Trial, hath not taken you, save such as man can bear; faithful, moreover is God, who will not suffer you to be tried above what ye are able, but will make, with the trial, also the way of escape, that ye may be able to hold out.
texts.1co.10.14: Wherefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry,—
texts.1co.10.15: As, to prudent men, I speak,—judge, ye, what I say:—
texts.1co.10.16: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not, a sharing together of the blood of the Christ? The loaf which we break, is it not, a sharing together of the body of the Christ?
texts.1co.10.17: Because, one loaf, one body, we, the many, are, for we, all, of the one loaf, partake.
texts.1co.10.18: Be looking at Israel after the flesh:—are not, they who eat the sacrifices, joint partakers with the altar?
texts.1co.10.19: What, then, am I saying?—that, an idol-sacrifice, is anything? or that, an idol, is anything?
texts.1co.10.20: On the contrary—that, the things which the nations sacrifice, unto demons, and not unto God, they sacrifice; and I wish not that ye should become, sharers together with the demons!
texts.1co.10.21: Ye cannot be drinking—a cup of the Lord, and a cup of demons; ye cannot be partaking of, a table of the Lord, and a table of demons.
texts.1co.10.22: Or are we to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we mightier than he?
texts.1co.10.23: All things are allowable—but, not all things, are profitable,—all things are allowable—but, not all things, upbuild.
texts.1co.10.24: Let, no one, be seeking, what concerneth himself, but that which concerneth some one else.
texts.1co.10.25: Whatsoever, in the market, is sold, eat,—asking no question, for conscience sake;
texts.1co.10.26: For, unto the Lord, belongeth the earth, and the fullness thereof.
texts.1co.10.27: If one of them who believe not invite you, and ye are disposed to go, whatsoever is set before you, eat,—asking no question, for conscience sake.
texts.1co.10.28: But, if anyone should say unto you,—This, is, a holy sacrifice, do not eat, for that man’s sake who disclosed it, and for conscience sake:—
texts.1co.10.29: But, conscience, I mean, not thine own, but the other’s,—for why is my freedom to be judged by another’s conscience?
texts.1co.10.30: If, I, with gratitude, partake, why am I to be defamed, as to that for which, I, give thanks?
texts.1co.10.31: Whether, therefore, ye eat or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do, all things to the glory of God.
texts.1co.10.32: Give no occasion of stumbling—whether to Jews, or to Greeks, or to the assembly of God:
texts.1co.10.33: Even as, I also, in all things do please all, not seeking my own profit, but that of the many, that they may be saved.
texts.1co.11.1: Become imitators of me,—even as, I also, [am] of Christ.
texts.1co.11.2: Now I praise you, that, in all things, ye have me in remembrance, and, even as I delivered unto you the instructions, ye hold them fast.
texts.1co.11.3: But I wish you to know—that, the head of every man, is, the Christ, and, the head of a woman, is, the man; and, the head of the Christ, is, God.
texts.1co.11.4: Every man, praying, or prophesying, having anything upon his head, putteth to shame his head;
texts.1co.11.5: But, every woman, praying, or prophesying, with her head, unveiled, putteth to shame her head,—for it is, one and the same, with her having been shaven.
texts.1co.11.6: For, if a woman doth not veil herself, let her also be shorn; but, if it were a shame in a woman to be shorn or shaven, let her be veiled.
texts.1co.11.7: For, a man, indeed, ought not to be veiling his head, being, the image and glory of God,—but, the woman, is the glory of man;
texts.1co.11.8: For, man, is not, of woman, but, woman, of man;
texts.1co.11.9: For also man was not created, for the sake of the woman, but woman, for the sake of the man.
texts.1co.11.10: For this cause, ought the woman to have, permission, upon her head, because of the messengers.
texts.1co.11.11: Howbeit, neither is woman apart from man, nor man apart from woman—in the Lord;
texts.1co.11.12: For, just as the woman is of the man, so, also the man, is through means of the woman;—but, all things, are of God.
texts.1co.11.13: Among your own selves, judge ye,—Is it becoming for a woman,—unveiled, to be praying unto God?
texts.1co.11.14: Doth not, even nature herself, teach you—that, if, a man, have long hair, it is a dishonour to him;
texts.1co.11.15: But, if, a woman, have long hair, it is a glory to her, for, her long hair, instead of a veil, hath been given to her.
texts.1co.11.16: But, if anyone thinketh to be contentious, we, have no such custom,—nor yet the assemblies of God.
texts.1co.11.17: But, in giving you the following charge, I praise you not,—in that, not for the better, but for the worse, ye come together.
texts.1co.11.18: For, first of all,—when ye come together in assembly, I hear that divisions among you exist,—and, in part, I believe it;
texts.1co.11.19: For there must needs be, even parties among you, that, the approved, [themselves] may become manifest among you.
texts.1co.11.20: When, therefore, ye come together into one place, it is not to eat, a supper unto the Lord;
texts.1co.11.21: For, each one, taketh beforehand, his own supper, in your eating, and, one, indeed, is hungry, whereas, another, is drinking to excess.
texts.1co.11.22: What! have ye not houses for your eating and drinking? or, the assembly of God, do ye despise, and, put to shame them who have nothing? What am I to say to you? Shall I praise you? In this, I praise you not.
texts.1co.11.23: For, I myself, received from the Lord—that which I also delivered unto you,—how that, the Lord Jesus, in the night in which he was being delivered up, took a loaf,
texts.1co.11.24: And, giving thanks, brake it, and said—This, is my body, which is for you,—this, do ye, in remembrance of me;
texts.1co.11.25: In the same manner, the cup also, after they had taken supper, saying—This cup, is, the new covenant in my blood, this, do ye, as often soever as ye may be drinking it, in remembrance of me.
texts.1co.11.26: For, as often as ye may be eating this loaf, and, the cup, may be drinking, The death of the Lord, do ye announce, until he come.
texts.1co.11.27: So that, whosoever may be eating the loaf, or drinking the cup of the Lord, in an unworthy manner, shall be responsible for the body and blood of the Lord.
texts.1co.11.28: But let a man be proving himself,—and, so, of the loaf, let him eat, and, of the cup, let him drink;
texts.1co.11.29: For, he that is eating and drinking,—judgment unto himself, doth eat and drink,—if he be not setting apart the body.
texts.1co.11.30: For this cause, many among you are weak and sickly; and, not a few, are falling asleep.
texts.1co.11.31: If, however, we had been setting, ourselves, apart, we had not, in that case, been coming under judgment;
texts.1co.11.32: But, being brought under judgment, by the Lord, are we being disciplined, lest, with the world, we should be condemned.
texts.1co.11.33: So then, my brethren,—when ye come together for the eating, unto one another, be giving welcome:—
texts.1co.11.34: If anyone be hungry, at home, let him eat, lest, unto judgment, ye be coming together. And, the remaining things, whensoever I come, I will set in order.
texts.1co.12.1: But, concerning the spiritually gifted, brethren, I am not wishing you to be ignorant.
texts.1co.12.2: Ye know that, when ye were of the nations, unto the dumb idols, howsoever ye were being led, ye were seduced.
texts.1co.12.3: Wherefore, I give you to know—that, no one, in God’s Spirit speaking, saith—Accursed Jesus! and, no one, can say—Lord Jesus! save in [the] Holy Spirit.
texts.1co.12.4: But, distributions of gifts, there are, yet the same Spirit,
texts.1co.12.5: And, distributions of ministries, there are, and the same Lord,
texts.1co.12.6: And, distributions of energies, there are, and the same God—who energiseth all things in all.
texts.1co.12.7: But, unto each one, is given the manifesting of the Spirit, with a view to that which is profitable;
texts.1co.12.8: For, unto one, indeed, through the Spirit, is given, a word of wisdom, but, unto another, a word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit;—
texts.1co.12.9: Unto a different one, faith, in the same Spirit, and, unto another, gifts of healings, in the one Spirit,
texts.1co.12.10: And, unto another, energies of mighty works, [and], unto another, prophesying, [and], unto another, discriminations of spirits,—unto a different one, kinds of tongues, and, unto another, translation of tongues;—
texts.1co.12.11: But, all these, energiseth the one and the same Spirit, distributing unto each one, peculiarly, even as it is disposed.
texts.1co.12.12: For, just as, the body, is one, and yet hath many members, but, all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so, also, the Christ;—
texts.1co.12.13: For, even to one Spirit, we all, into one body, have been immersed,—whether Jews or Greeks, whether bond or free,—and, all, of one Spirit, have been caused to drink.
texts.1co.12.14: For, the body also, is not one member, but many:
texts.1co.12.15: Though the foot should say—Because I am not a hand, I am not of the body, Is it, therefore, not, of the body?
texts.1co.12.16: And, though the ear should say—Because I am not an eye, I am not of the body, Is it, therefore, not, of the body?
texts.1co.12.17: If, the whole body, were, an eye, where were the hearing? If, the whole were, hearing, where were, the smelling?
texts.1co.12.18: But, now, hath God set the members, each one of them in the body, even as he pleased.
texts.1co.12.19: But, if they all had been one member, Where had been, the body?
texts.1co.12.20: Now, however there are many members, yet one body;
texts.1co.12.21: [And] the eye cannot say unto the hand—I have no need of thee,—nor, again, the head, unto the feet—I have no need of you:—
texts.1co.12.22: Nay! much more, the members which seem to be weaker are necessary,
texts.1co.12.23: And, the parts of the body which we deem to be less honourable, on these, more abundant honour, do we bestow, and, our uncomely parts, have, more abundant comeliness,
texts.1co.12.24: Whereas, our comely parts, have, no need. But, God, hath tempered the body together,—unto that which was lacking, giving more abundant honour;—
texts.1co.12.25: That there might be no division in the body, but that the members might have, the same, care, one for another;
texts.1co.12.26: And, whether one member, suffereth, all the members, suffer with it, or, a member is glorified, all the members, rejoice together.
texts.1co.12.27: Now, ye, are the body of Christ, and members severally;—
texts.1co.12.28: And God hath, indeed, set, certain, in the assembly,—first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, after that mighty works, then gifts of healings, helps, guidings, kinds of tongues.
texts.1co.12.29: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all mighty works?
texts.1co.12.30: Have, all, gifts of healings? Do, all, with tongues, speak? Do, all, translate?
texts.1co.12.31: Be envious, however, of the greater gifts; and, yet, a much more excellent way, unto you, I point out:—
texts.1co.13.1: Although with the tongues of men, I be speaking, and of messengers, and have not, love, I have become resounding brass, or a clanging cymbal;
texts.1co.13.2: And, though I have [the gift of] prophesying, and know all sacred secrets, and all knowledge,—and though I have all faith, so as to be removing mountains, and have not, love, I am, nothing;
texts.1co.13.3: And, though I morsel out all my goods,—and though I deliver up my body, that I may boast, and have not, love, I am profited, nothing.
texts.1co.13.4: Love, is patient, is gracious. Love, is not envious, vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,
texts.1co.13.5: Acteth not unbecomingly, seeketh not her own things, is not easily provoked, imputeth not that which is base,
texts.1co.13.6: Rejoiceth not over unrighteousness, but rejoiceth in sympathy with truth,—
texts.1co.13.7: All things, covereth, all things, believeth, all things, hopeth, all things, endureth.
texts.1co.13.8: Love, at no time, faileth;—but, whether prophesyings, they shall be done away, whether tongues, they shall cease, whether gaining knowledge, it shall be done away;
texts.1co.13.9: For, in part, are we gaining knowledge, and, in part, are we prophesying,—
texts.1co.13.10: But, as soon as that which is complete is come, that which is in part, shall be done away.
texts.1co.13.11: When I was a child, I used to speak as a child, to prefer as child, to reason as a child: now I have become a man, I have laid aside the things of the child!
texts.1co.13.12: For we see, as yet, through a dim window, obscurely, but, then, face to face: as yet, I gain knowledge, in part, but, then, shall I fully know, even as I was also fully known.
texts.1co.13.13: But, now abide—faith, hope, love,—these three; but, the greatest of these, is, love.
texts.1co.14.1: Pursue love; nevertheless be envious of the spiritual gifts,—and, rather, that ye may be prophesying.
texts.1co.14.2: For, he that speaketh with a tongue, not unto men, doth speak, but, unto God,—for, no one, understandeth, although, in spirit, he is speaking sacred secrets;
texts.1co.14.3: But, be that prophesieth, unto men, doth speak—edification, and exhortation, and comfort.
texts.1co.14.4: He that speaketh with a tongue, buildeth up, himself, whereas, he that prophesieth, buildeth up, an assembly.
texts.1co.14.5: Howbeit I wish you all to speak with tongues, but, rather, that ye may prophesy,—moreover, greater, is he that prophesieth, than he that speaketh with tongues,—unless indeed he translate, that, the assembly, may receive upbuilding.
texts.1co.14.6: But, now, brethren—if I come unto you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit, you, except I speak, unto you, either by way of revelation, or knowledge, or prophesying, or teaching?
texts.1co.14.7: In like manner, the things without life giving sound, whether pipe or harp, if, a distinction in the sounds, they do not give, how shall it be known, what is being piped or harped?
texts.1co.14.8: For, if also, an uncertain sound, a trumpet, should give, who shall prepare himself for battle?
texts.1co.14.9: So, also, ye, through means of the tongue, except ye give intelligible discourse, how shall it be known what is being spoken? for ye will be speaking, to the air.
texts.1co.14.10: There may happen to be so many kinds of languages in the world, and, not one, unspoken:—
texts.1co.14.11: If, then, I do not know the meaning of the language, I shall be, unto him that is speaking, a foreigner, and, he that is speaking, shall be, in my case, a foreigner.
texts.1co.14.12: So, ye, also—since ye are, envious, of spirits, unto the upbuilding of the assembly, seek to be pre-eminent.
texts.1co.14.13: Wherefore, he that speaketh with a tongue, let him pray that he may translate;
texts.1co.14.14: [For], if I am praying in a tongue, my spirit, is praying, but, my mind, is unfruitful.
texts.1co.14.15: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, but I will pray also with the mind,—I will strike the strings with the spirit, [but] I will strike the strings also with the mind.
texts.1co.14.16: Else, if thou be blessing in a spirit, he that filleth up the place of the ungifted person, how shall he say the Amen upon thy thanksgiving? since indeed, what thou art saying, he knoweth not;
texts.1co.14.17: For, thou, indeed, excellently art giving thanks, but, the other, is not being built up.
texts.1co.14.18: I give thanks unto God!—More than ye all, am I speaking with tongues;
texts.1co.14.19: But, in assembly, I desire to speak five words with my mind, that, others also, I may instruct, than myriads of words in a tongue.
texts.1co.14.20: Brethren! do not become children, in your understandings; but, in baseness, become babes, while, in your understandings, ye become, full-grown.
texts.1co.14.21: In the law, it is written—With strange tongues, and with lips of strangers, will I speak unto this people; and, not even so, will they hearken unto me,—saith the Lord.
texts.1co.14.22: So that, the tongues, are for a sign—not unto them that believe, but, unto them that believe not; whereas, prophesying, is not for them that believe not, but, for them that believe.
texts.1co.14.23: If, then, the whole assembly come together with one consent, and, all, are speaking with tongues,—and there come in persons unskilled or unbelieving, will they not say that ye are raving?
texts.1co.14.24: But, if, all, be prophesying,—and there come in one who is unbelieving or unskilled, he is convicted by all, he is searched by all, the secrets of his heart, become manifest,
texts.1co.14.25: And, so, falling down upon his face, he will do homage unto God, reporting that, in reality, God is, among you.
texts.1co.14.26: What, then, is it, brethren? Whensoever ye are coming together, each one, hath a psalm, hath a teaching, hath a revelation, hath a tongue, hath a translation:—let, all things, be done, unto building up.
texts.1co.14.27: If, with a tongue, one is speaking, let it be by two, or, at the most, three,—and by turns; and let, one, be translating;
texts.1co.14.28: But, if there be none to translate, let him keep silence in assembly, and, unto himself, be speaking, and, unto God!
texts.1co.14.29: Prophets, moreover, let two or three speak, and let, the others, judge.
texts.1co.14.30: If, however, unto another, a revelation be made, as he is sitting, let the first be silent;
texts.1co.14.31: For, one by one, ye can, all, be prophesying,—that, all, may learn, and, all, be encouraged.
texts.1co.14.32: And, spirits of prophets, unto prophets, do submit themselves;
texts.1co.14.33: For God is not [a God] of confusion, but, of peace:—as in all the assemblies of the saints.
texts.1co.14.34: As for the women, in the assemblies, let them be silent, for it is not permitted them to be speaking; but let them be in submission,—even as, the law, saith.
texts.1co.14.35: If, however, they are wishing to learn something, at home, their own husbands, let them question; for it is a shame for a woman to be speaking in assembly.
texts.1co.14.36: Or, from you, did the word of God come forth? Or, unto you alone, did it extend?
texts.1co.14.37: If anyone thinketh himself to be a prophet, or spiritually gifted, let him acknowledge the things which I am writing to you,—that they are, a commandment, of the Lord.
texts.1co.14.38: But, if anyone knoweth not, he is unknown!
texts.1co.14.39: So, then, my brethren,—be zealous to prophesy, and do not forbid, to be speaking with tongues;
texts.1co.14.40: But let, all things, with comeliness, and by arrangement, be done.
texts.1co.15.1: Moreover, brethren, I make known unto you The joyful message, which I myself announced to you, which also ye received, in which also ye stand;
texts.1co.15.2: Through which also ye are being saved,—if ye hold fast, with what discourse, I announced the joyful message unto you; unless indeed, in vain, ye believed.
texts.1co.15.3: For I delivered unto you, among the first things, what also I received:—how that Christ died for our sins, according to the Scriptures,
texts.1co.15.4: And that he was buried, and that he hath been raised, on the third day, according to the Scriptures,—
texts.1co.15.5: And that he appeared unto Cephas, then, to the twelve,
texts.1co.15.6: After that, he appeared to above five hundred brethren at once,—of whom, the greater number, remain until even now, but, some, have fallen asleep,—
texts.1co.15.7: After that, he appeared unto James, then, unto all the apostles,
texts.1co.15.8: And, last of all, just as if unto the unseasonable birth, he appeared, even unto me;
texts.1co.15.9: For, I, am the least of the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the assembly of God.
texts.1co.15.10: But, by favour of God, I am what I am, and, his favour, which was unto me, hath not been made void,—but, much more abundantly than they all, have I toiled, albeit not, I, but the favour of God with me.
texts.1co.15.11: Whether therefore, I, or, they, thus do we proclaim, and, thus did ye believe.
texts.1co.15.12: Now, if, Christ is proclaimed, that, from among the dead, he hath been raised, how say some, among you—resurrection of the dead, there is none?
texts.1co.15.13: But, if, resurrection of the dead, there is none, not even Christ, hath been raised;
texts.1co.15.14: And, if Christ, hath not been raised, void, after all, is our proclamation, void also, our faith,—
texts.1co.15.15: And we are found, even false-witnesses of God, because we have witnessed respecting God, that he raised the Christ,—whom he did not raise, if, indeed, after all, the dead are not raised!
texts.1co.15.16: For, if the dead are not raised, not even Christ, hath been raised;
texts.1co.15.17: And, if Christ hath not been raised, to no purpose, is your faith, yet, are ye in your sins!
texts.1co.15.18: Hence also, they who are fallen asleep in Christ, are lost:
texts.1co.15.19: If, in this life, in Christ, we have hoped—and that is all, we are, of all men, most to be pitied.
texts.1co.15.20: But, now, hath Christ been raised from among the dead,—a firstfruit of them who have fallen asleep;
texts.1co.15.21: For, since indeed, through a man, came death, through a man, also cometh the raising of the dead;
texts.1co.15.22: For, just as, in the Adam, all die, so, also, in the Christ, shall all be made alive.
texts.1co.15.23: But, each, in his own rank:—A firstfruit, Christ, after that, they who are the Christ’s, in his presence,
texts.1co.15.24: Afterwards, the end—whensoever he delivereth up the kingdom unto his God and Father, whensoever he shall bring to nought all rule and all authority and power;
texts.1co.15.25: For he must needs reign, until he shall put all his enemies under his feet:
texts.1co.15.26: As a last enemy, death, is to be destroyed;
texts.1co.15.27: For—He put, all things, in subjection under his feet. But, whensoever it shall be said—all things are in subjection!—it is evident that it means,—Except him who did put into subjection, unto him, the all things—
texts.1co.15.28: But whensoever have been put into subjection, unto him, the all things, then, the Son himself, [also] shall be put in subjection unto him who put in subjection, unto him, the all things,—that, God, may be, all things in all.
texts.1co.15.29: Else, what will they do, who are being immersed in behalf of the dead? If, not at all, are the dead to be raised, why are they even being immersed in their behalf?
texts.1co.15.30: Why also are, we, running into peril every hour?
texts.1co.15.31: Day by day, am I dying!—Yea! by your own boasting, brethren, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
texts.1co.15.32: If, after the manner of men, I have fought with wild-beasts at Ephesus, what, to me, the profit? If the dead are not raised, Let us eat and drink, for, tomorrow, we die.
texts.1co.15.33: Be not deceiving yourselves,—evil communications corrupt gentle manners:—
texts.1co.15.34: Wake up to sobriety, in righteousness, and be not committing sin; for some have, an ignorance of God: for shame, unto you, am I speaking!
texts.1co.15.35: But some one will say—How, are the dead raised? and, with what kind of body, do they come?
texts.1co.15.36: Simple one! What, thou, sowest, is not quickened, except it die;
texts.1co.15.37: And, what thou sowest, not the body that shall come into existence, dost thou sow, but a naked kernel—if it so happen, of wheat, or of any of the rest,—
texts.1co.15.38: Howbeit, God, giveth it a body, as he pleased, and, unto each of the seeds, a body of its own.
texts.1co.15.39: Not all flesh, is the same flesh; but, one, indeed, is, [the flesh] of men, and, another, the flesh of beasts, and, another, the flesh of birds, and, another, of fishes;
texts.1co.15.40: And there are heavenly bodies, and earthly bodies,—but, of one kind, indeed, is the glory of the heavenly, and, of another kind, is the glory of the earthly;—
texts.1co.15.41: One, is the glory of a sun, and, another, the glory of a moon, and, another, the glory of stars,—nay! star from star, differeth in glory.
texts.1co.15.42: Thus, also the resurrection of the dead: it is sown in corruption, it is raised in incorruption,
texts.1co.15.43: It is sown in dishonour, it is raised in glory, it is sown in weakness, it is raised in power,
texts.1co.15.44: It is sown a body of the soul, it is raised a body of the spirit; if there is a body of the soul, there is also of the spirit:—
texts.1co.15.45: Thus, also, it is written—The first man, Adam, became, a living soul, the last Adam, a life-giving spirit.
texts.1co.15.46: Howbeit, not first, is the [body] of the spirit, but that, of the soul,—afterwards, that of the spirit.
texts.1co.15.47: The first man, is of the ground, earthy, the second man, is, of heaven:
texts.1co.15.48: As, the man of earth, such, also, the men of earth, and, as, the man of heaven, such, also, the men of heaven;
texts.1co.15.49: And, even as we have borne the image of the man of earth, let us also bear the image of the man of heaven.
texts.1co.15.50: And, this, I say, brethren,—that, flesh and blood, cannot inherit, God’s kingdom. Neither doth, corruption, inherit, incorruption.
texts.1co.15.51: Lo! a sacred secret, unto you, do I declare:—we shall not, all, sleep, but we shall, all, be changed,—
texts.1co.15.52: In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, during the last trumpet; for it shall sound, and, the dead, shall be raised, incorruptible, and, we, shall be changed.
texts.1co.15.53: For this corruptible must needs clothe itself with incorruptibility, and this mortal, clothe itself, with immortality.
texts.1co.15.54: But, whensoever, this mortal, shall clothe itself with immortality, then, shall be brought to pass the saying that is written—Death hath been swallowed up, victoriously;
texts.1co.15.55: Where, O death, is thy victory? Where, O death, is thy sting?
texts.1co.15.56: Now, the sting of death, is, sin, and, the power of sin, is, the law;—
texts.1co.15.57: But, unto God, be thanks, who is giving unto us the victory, through our Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.1co.15.58: So, then, my beloved brethren,—become ye, steadfast, immovable, superabounding in the work of the Lord, at all times; knowing that, your toil, is not in vain in the Lord.
texts.1co.16.1: Now, concerning the collection which is for the saints, just as I directed the assemblies of Galatia, so, also do, ye:—
texts.1co.16.2: Upon the first of the week, let, each one of you, put, by itself, in store, as he may be prospering,—lest, as soon as I come, then, collections, should be in progress.
texts.1co.16.3: And, as soon as I arrive, whomsoever ye shall approve by letters, these, will I send, to bear away your favour unto Jerusalem:
texts.1co.16.4: And, if it be meet that, I also, be journeying, with me, shall they journey.
texts.1co.16.5: Now I will come unto you, as soon as I have passed through Macedonia,—for I do pass through Macedonia,
texts.1co.16.6: And, with you, I may perhaps sojourn, or winter, that, ye, may set me forward, whithersoever I may be journeying.
texts.1co.16.7: For I do not wish to see you, just now, by the way; for I hope to remain, some time, with you,—if, the Lord, permit.
texts.1co.16.8: But I remain in Ephesus, until the Pentecost,
texts.1co.16.9: For, a door, unto me, hath opened, great and effectual, and, opposers, are many.
texts.1co.16.10: But, if Timothy should come, see that, without fear, he be with you, for, in the work of the Lord, doth he labour, even as, I:
texts.1co.16.11: Let no one then despise him; and set ye him forward in peace, that he may come unto me, for I expect him with the brethren.
texts.1co.16.12: But, concerning Apollos the brother, much, did I beseech him, that he would come unto you, with the brethren, but there was, by no means, any will, that he should come, now;—he will come, however, as soon as he hath good opportunity.
texts.1co.16.13: Be on the watch, stand firm in the faith, be men—be strong;
texts.1co.16.14: Let, all your affairs, in love, be carried on.
texts.1co.16.15: Now I beseech you, brethren,—ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is a first-fruit of Achaia, and, for the purpose of ministering, they devoted themselves, unto the saints—
texts.1co.16.16: That, ye also, be submitting yourselves unto such as these,—and unto everyone helping in the work and toiling.
texts.1co.16.17: I Rejoice, moreover, in the presence of Stephanas, and Fortunatus, and Achaicus: because, your own shortcoming, these, have filled up:—
texts.1co.16.18: They have given rest, in fact, unto my spirit, and yours: hold in acknowledgment, therefore, such as these.
texts.1co.16.19: The assemblies of Asia salute you: Aquila and Priscilla, with the assembly meeting at their house, salute you much in the Lord:
texts.1co.16.20: All the brethren salute you:—Salute ye one another with a holy kiss.
texts.1co.16.21: The salutation of Paul—with my own hand.
texts.1co.16.22: If anyone doth not dearly love the Lord, let him be anathema [that is, "accursed"]: Maran atha [that is, "The Lord, cometh"].
texts.1co.16.23: The favour of the Lord Jesus, be with you.
texts.1co.16.24: My love, be with you all, in Christ Jesus.

texts.1co.1.1: Pablo, llamado a ser apóstol de Jesucristo por la voluntad de Dios, y nuestro hermano Sóstenes,
texts.1co.1.2: a la asamblea de Dios que está en Corinto: los santificados en Cristo Jesús, llamados santos, con todos los que invocan el nombre de nuestro Señor Jesucristo en todo lugar, tanto de ellos como de nosotros:
texts.1co.1.3: Gracia a vosotros y paz de parte de Dios nuestro Padre y del Señor Jesucristo.
texts.1co.1.4: Siempre doy gracias a mi Dios respecto a vosotros por la gracia de Dios que os fue dada en Cristo Jesús,
texts.1co.1.5: que en todo fuisteis enriquecidos en él, en toda palabra y en toda sabiduría,
texts.1co.1.6: así como el testimonio de Cristo fue confirmado en vosotros,
texts.1co.1.7: para que no os quedéis atrás en ningún don, esperando la revelación de nuestro Señor Jesucristo,
texts.1co.1.8: que también os confirmará hasta el fin, irreprochables en el día de nuestro Señor Jesucristo.
texts.1co.1.9: Fiel es Dios, por quien fuisteis llamados a la comunión de su Hijo Jesucristo, nuestro Señor.
texts.1co.1.10: Ahora os ruego, hermanos, por el nombre de nuestro Señor Jesucristo, que habléis todos una misma cosa, y que no haya divisiones entre vosotros, sino que os perfeccionéis juntos en una misma mente y en un mismo juicio.
texts.1co.1.11: Porque se me ha informado acerca de vosotros, hermanos míos, por parte de los que son de la casa de Cloe, que hay disputas entre vosotros.
texts.1co.1.12: Quiero decir que cada uno de vosotros dice: «Yo sigo a Pablo», «Yo sigo a Apolos», «Yo sigo a Cefas» y «Yo sigo a Cristo».
texts.1co.1.13: ¿Está dividido Cristo? ¿Fue Pablo crucificado por vosotros? ¿O fuisteis bautizados en el nombre de Pablo?
texts.1co.1.14: Doy gracias a Dios porque no bauticé a ninguno de vosotros, excepto a Crispo y a Gayo,
texts.1co.1.15: para que nadie diga que os bauticé en mi propio nombre.
texts.1co.1.16: (También bauticé a la casa de Estéfanas; además de ellos, no sé si bauticé a algún otro).
texts.1co.1.17: Porque Cristo no me ha enviado a bautizar, sino a predicar la Buena Nueva, no con sabiduría de palabras, para que la cruz de Cristo no sea anulada.
texts.1co.1.18: Porque la palabra de la cruz es una tontería para los que mueren, pero para los que se salvan es poder de Dios.
texts.1co.1.19: Porque está escrito, «Destruiré la sabiduría de los sabios. Haré que el discernimiento de los perspicaces quede en nada».
texts.1co.1.20: ¿Dónde está el sabio? ¿Dónde está el escriba? ¿Dónde está el polemista de este siglo? ¿Acaso Dios no ha hecho insensata la sabiduría de este mundo?
texts.1co.1.21: Pues viendo que en la sabiduría de Dios, el mundo por su sabiduría no conoció a Dios, a Dios le agradó salvar a los creyentes por medio de la locura de la predicación.
texts.1co.1.22: Porque los judíos piden señales, los griegos buscan sabiduría,
texts.1co.1.23: pero nosotros predicamos a Cristo crucificado, escándalo para los judíos y necedad para los griegos,
texts.1co.1.24: pero para los llamados, tanto judíos como griegos, Cristo es poder de Dios y sabiduría de Dios;
texts.1co.1.25: porque la necedad de Dios es más sabia que los hombres, y la debilidad de Dios es más fuerte que los hombres.
texts.1co.1.26: Porque ya veis vuestra vocación, hermanos, que no hay muchos sabios según la carne, ni muchos poderosos, ni muchos nobles;
texts.1co.1.27: sino que Dios eligió lo necio del mundo para avergonzar a los sabios. Dios eligió a los débiles del mundo para avergonzar a los fuertes.
texts.1co.1.28: Dios eligió lo humilde del mundo, lo despreciable y lo que no existe, para reducir a la nada lo que existe,
texts.1co.1.29: a fin de que nadie se jacte ante Dios.
texts.1co.1.30: Porque por él estáis en Cristo Jesús, que nos fue hecho sabiduría de Dios, y justicia y santificación, y redención,
texts.1co.1.31: para que, como está escrito: «El que se gloríe, que se gloríe en el Señor».
texts.1co.2.1: Cuando fui a vosotros, hermanos, no fui con excelencia de palabra o de sabiduría, anunciándoos el testimonio de Dios.
texts.1co.2.2: Porque me propuse no conocer nada entre vosotros, sino a Jesucristo y a éste crucificado.
texts.1co.2.3: Estuve con vosotros con debilidad, con temor y con mucho temblor.
texts.1co.2.4: Mi discurso y mi predicación no fueron con palabras persuasivas de sabiduría humana, sino con la demostración del Espíritu y del poder,
texts.1co.2.5: para que vuestra fe no permaneciera en la sabiduría de los hombres, sino en el poder de Dios.
texts.1co.2.6: Sin embargo, hablamos de la sabiduría de los que ya han crecido, pero una sabiduría que no es de este mundo ni de los gobernantes de este mundo que están llegando a la nada.
texts.1co.2.7: Pero hablamos la sabiduría de Dios en un misterio, la sabiduría que ha estado oculta, que Dios preordenó antes de los mundos para nuestra gloria,
texts.1co.2.8: que ninguno de los gobernantes de este mundo ha conocido. Porque si la hubieran conocido, no habrían crucificado al Señor de la gloria.
texts.1co.2.9: Pero como está escrito, «Cosas que un ojo no vio, y un oído no oyó, que no entró en el corazón del hombre, que Dios ha preparado para los que le aman».
texts.1co.2.10: Pero a nosotros, Dios nos las reveló por medio del Espíritu. Porque el Espíritu escudriña todas las cosas, sí, las cosas profundas de Dios.
texts.1co.2.11: Porque ¿quién de los hombres conoce las cosas del hombre sino el espíritu del hombre que está en él? Así, nadie conoce las cosas de Dios sino el Espíritu de Dios.
texts.1co.2.12: Pero nosotros no hemos recibido el espíritu del mundo, sino el Espíritu que viene de Dios, para conocer las cosas que nos han sido dadas gratuitamente por Dios.
texts.1co.2.13: También hablamos estas cosas, no con las palabras que enseña la sabiduría de los hombres, sino con las que enseña el Espíritu Santo, comparando las cosas espirituales con las espirituales.
texts.1co.2.14: Ahora bien, el hombre natural no recibe las cosas del Espíritu de Dios, porque para él son locura, y no puede conocerlas, porque se disciernen espiritualmente.
texts.1co.2.15: Pero el que es espiritual discierne todas las cosas, y no debe ser juzgado por nadie.
texts.1co.2.16: «Porque ¿quién ha conocido la mente del Señor para instruirlo?» Pero nosotros tenemos la mente de Cristo.
texts.1co.3.1: Hermanos, no podía hablaros como a espirituales, sino como a carnales, como a bebés en Cristo.
texts.1co.3.2: Os he alimentado con leche, no con alimentos sólidos, porque aún no estabais preparados. De hecho, no estáis preparados ni siquiera ahora,
texts.1co.3.3: porque todavía sois carnales. Porque en cuanto a los celos, las disputas y las facciones entre vosotros, ¿no sois carnales y no andáis por los caminos de los hombres?
texts.1co.3.4: Porque cuando uno dice: «Yo sigo a Pablo», y otro: «Yo sigo a Apolos», ¿no sois carnales?
texts.1co.3.5: ¿Quién es, pues, Apolos y quién Pablo, sino servidores por medio de los cuales creísteis, y cada uno según le dio el Señor?
texts.1co.3.6: Yo planté. Apolos regó. Pero el crecimiento lo dio Dios.
texts.1co.3.7: Así que ni el que planta es algo, ni el que riega, sino Dios que da el crecimiento.
texts.1co.3.8: Ahora bien, el que planta y el que riega son lo mismo, pero cada uno recibirá su propia recompensa según su trabajo.
texts.1co.3.9: Porque nosotros somos colaboradores de Dios. Vosotros sois labradores de Dios, constructores de Dios.
texts.1co.3.10: Según la gracia de Dios que me fue concedida, como sabio maestro de obras puse un fundamento, y otro construye sobre él. Pero que cada uno tenga cuidado de cómo construye sobre él.
texts.1co.3.11: Porque nadie puede poner otro fundamento que el que está puesto, que es Jesucristo.
texts.1co.3.12: Pero si alguien construye sobre el fundamento con oro, plata, piedras preciosas, madera, heno o paja,
texts.1co.3.13: la obra de cada uno será revelada. Porque el Día lo declarará, porque se revela en el fuego; y el fuego mismo probará qué clase de obra es la de cada uno.
texts.1co.3.14: Si la obra de algún hombre permanece lo que construyó, recibirá una recompensa.
texts.1co.3.15: Si la obra de alguno se quema, sufrirá pérdida, pero él mismo se salvará, pero como a través del fuego.
texts.1co.3.16: ¿No sabéis que vosotros sois el templo de Dios y que el Espíritu de Dios vive en vosotros?
texts.1co.3.17: Si alguien destruye el templo de Dios, Dios lo destruirá a él, porque el templo de Dios, que vosotros sois, es santo.
texts.1co.3.18: Que nadie se engañe a sí mismo. Si alguno se cree sabio entre vosotros en este mundo, que se haga tonto para llegar a ser sabio.
texts.1co.3.19: Porque la sabiduría de este mundo es una tontería para Dios. Porque está escrito: «Él ha tomado a los sabios en su astucia».
texts.1co.3.20: Y también: «El Señor conoce el razonamiento de los sabios, que es inútil».
texts.1co.3.21: Por tanto, que nadie se jacte en los hombres. Porque todas las cosas son vuestras,
texts.1co.3.22: ya sea Pablo, o Apolos, o Cefas, o el mundo, o la vida, o la muerte, o las cosas presentes, o las cosas por venir. Todo es vuestro,
texts.1co.3.23: y vosotros sois de Cristo, y Cristo es de Dios.
texts.1co.4.1: Así pues, que el hombre piense en nosotros como servidores de Cristo y administradores de los misterios de Dios.
texts.1co.4.2: Aquí, además, se exige a los administradores que sean hallados fieles.
texts.1co.4.3: Pero para mí es una cosa muy pequeña que me juzguéis vosotros o un tribunal humano. Sí, ni siquiera me juzgo a mí mismo.
texts.1co.4.4: Porque nada sé contra mí mismo. Pero no me justifico por esto, sino que el que me juzga es el Señor.
texts.1co.4.5: Por tanto, no juzguéis nada antes de tiempo, hasta que venga el Señor, que sacará a la luz lo oculto de las tinieblas y revelará los designios de los corazones. Entonces cada uno recibirá su alabanza de Dios.
texts.1co.4.6: Ahora bien, estas cosas, hermanos, las he transferido en figura a mí mismo y a Apolos por vosotros, para que en nosotros aprendáis a no pensar más allá de lo que está escrito, para que ninguno de vosotros se ensoberbezca contra el otro.
texts.1co.4.7: Porque ¿quién os hace diferentes? ¿Y qué tenéis que no hayáis recibido? Pero si lo habéis recibido, ¿por qué os jactáis como si no lo hubierais recibido?
texts.1co.4.8: Ya estáis llenos. Ya os habéis enriquecido. Habéis comenzado a reinar sin nosotros. Sí, ¡y yo quisiera que reinarais, para que también nosotros reináramos con vosotros!
texts.1co.4.9: Porque pienso que Dios nos ha exhibido a nosotros, los apóstoles, los últimos, como hombres condenados a muerte. Porque somos un espectáculo para el mundo, tanto para los ángeles como para los hombres.
texts.1co.4.10: Nosotros somos tontos por causa de Cristo, pero vosotros sois sabios en Cristo. Nosotros somos débiles, pero vosotros sois fuertes. Vosotros tenéis honor, pero nosotros tenemos deshonra.
texts.1co.4.11: Hasta esta hora tenemos hambre, sed, estamos desnudos, somos golpeados y no tenemos una morada segura.
texts.1co.4.12: Nos esforzamos, trabajando con nuestras propias manos. Cuando la gente nos maldice, nosotros bendecimos. Si nos persiguen, aguantamos.
texts.1co.4.13: Cuando nos difaman, suplicamos. Estamos hechos como la inmundicia del mundo, la suciedad limpiada por todos, incluso hasta ahora.
texts.1co.4.14: No escribo estas cosas para avergonzaros, sino para amonestaros como a mis hijos amados.
texts.1co.4.15: Porque aunque tengáis diez mil tutores en Cristo, no tenéis muchos padres. Porque en Cristo Jesús me convertí en vuestro padre por la Buena Nueva.
texts.1co.4.16: Os ruego, pues, que seáis imitadores míos.
texts.1co.4.17: Por eso os he enviado a Timoteo, que es mi hijo amado y fiel en el Señor, el cual os recordará mis caminos que son en Cristo, así como yo enseño en todas las asambleas.
texts.1co.4.18: Ahora bien, algunos se envanecen, como si yo no fuera a vosotros.
texts.1co.4.19: Pero iré pronto a vosotros, si el Señor quiere. Y conoceré, no la palabra de los engreídos, sino el poder.
texts.1co.4.20: Porque el Reino de Dios no es de palabra, sino de poder.
texts.1co.4.21: ¿Qué queréis? ¿Voy a ir a vosotros con vara, o con amor y espíritu de mansedumbre?
texts.1co.5.1: En realidad, se dice que hay inmoralidad sexual entre vosotros, y una inmoralidad sexual como no se nombra entre los gentiles, que uno tiene la mujer de su padre.
texts.1co.5.2: Vosotros sois arrogantes y no os habéis lamentado, en cambio, de que el que ha hecho este acto sea eliminado de entre vosotros.
texts.1co.5.3: Porque ciertamente, como ausente en cuerpo pero presente en espíritu, ya he juzgado, como si estuviera presente, al que ha hecho esto.
texts.1co.5.4: En el nombre de nuestro Señor Jesucristo, cuando os reunáis con mi espíritu con el poder de nuestro Señor Jesucristo,
texts.1co.5.5: debéis entregar al tal a Satanás para la destrucción de la carne, a fin de que el espíritu se salve en el día del Señor Jesús.
texts.1co.5.6: Vuestra jactancia no es buena. ¿No sabéis que un poco de levadura leuda toda la masa?
texts.1co.5.7: Limpiad la levadura vieja, para que seáis una masa nueva, así como sin levadura. Porque, en efecto, Cristo, nuestra Pascua, ha sido sacrificado en nuestro lugar.
texts.1co.5.8: Por tanto, celebremos la fiesta, no con la levadura vieja, ni con la levadura de la malicia y de la maldad, sino con el pan sin levadura de la sinceridad y de la verdad.
texts.1co.5.9: Os escribí en mi carta que no os juntarais con los pecadores sexuales;
texts.1co.5.10: pero no me refiero en absoluto a los pecadores sexuales de este mundo, ni a los avaros y extorsionadores, ni a los idólatras, porque entonces tendríais que dejar el mundo.
texts.1co.5.11: Pero tal como es, os escribí que no os juntéis con ninguno de los llamados hermanos que sean pecadores sexuales, o codiciosos, o idólatras, o calumniadores, o borrachos, o extorsionistas. Ni siquiera comáis con una persona así.
texts.1co.5.12: Porque, ¿qué tengo yo que ver con juzgar también a los que están fuera? ¿No juzgáis vosotros a los que están dentro?
texts.1co.5.13: Pero a los que están fuera, Dios los juzga. «Quitad al malvado de entre vosotros».
texts.1co.6.1: ¿Se atreve alguno de vosotros, teniendo un asunto contra su prójimo, a acudir a la justicia ante los injustos, y no ante los santos?
texts.1co.6.2: ¿No sabéis que los santos juzgarán al mundo? Y si el mundo es juzgado por vosotros, ¿sois indignos de juzgar los asuntos más pequeños?
texts.1co.6.3: ¿No sabéis que nosotros juzgaremos a los ángeles? ¿Cuánto más las cosas que pertenecen a esta vida?
texts.1co.6.4: Si, pues, tenéis que juzgar las cosas que pertenecen a esta vida, ¿los ponéis a juzgar a los que no tienen importancia en la asamblea?
texts.1co.6.5: Digo esto para avergonzaros. ¿No hay entre vosotros ni siquiera un sabio que pueda decidir entre sus hermanos?
texts.1co.6.6: ¡Pero el hermano va a juicio con el hermano, y eso ante los incrédulos!
texts.1co.6.7: Por lo tanto, ya es un defecto en vosotros que tengáis pleitos unos con otros. ¿Por qué no ser más bien agraviados? ¿Por qué no ser más bien defraudados?
texts.1co.6.8: No, sino que vosotros mismos hacéis mal y defraudáis, y eso contra vuestros hermanos.
texts.1co.6.9: ¿O es que no sabéis que los injustos no heredarán el Reino de Dios? No os engañéis. Ni los inmorales, ni los idólatras, ni los adúlteros, ni las prostitutas, ni los homosexuales,
texts.1co.6.10: ni los ladrones, ni los avaros, ni los borrachos, ni los calumniadores, ni los extorsionistas, heredarán el Reino de Dios.
texts.1co.6.11: Algunos de vosotros erais así, pero fuisteis lavados. Fuisteis santificados. Fuisteis justificados en el nombre del Señor Jesús y en el Espíritu de nuestro Dios.
texts.1co.6.12: «Todo me es lícito», pero no todo es conveniente. «Todas las cosas me son lícitas», pero no me someteré al poder de nada.
texts.1co.6.13: «Alimentos para el vientre, y el vientre para los alimentos», pero Dios hará desaparecer tanto a él como a ellos. Pero el cuerpo no es para la inmoralidad sexual, sino para el Señor, y el Señor para el cuerpo.
texts.1co.6.14: Ahora bien, Dios resucitó al Señor, y también nos resucitará a nosotros con su poder.
texts.1co.6.15: ¿No sabéis que vuestros cuerpos son miembros de Cristo? ¿Acaso voy a tomar los miembros de Cristo para hacerlos miembros de una prostituta? ¡Que nunca sea así!
texts.1co.6.16: ¿Acaso no sabéis que el que se une a una prostituta es un solo cuerpo? Porque, «Los dos», dice, «se convertirán en una sola carne».
texts.1co.6.17: Pero el que se une al Señor es un solo espíritu.
texts.1co.6.18: ¡Huid de la inmoralidad sexual! «Todo pecado que el hombre hace está fuera del cuerpo», pero el que comete inmoralidad sexual peca contra su propio cuerpo.
texts.1co.6.19: ¿O no sabéis que vuestro cuerpo es templo del Espíritu Santo que está en vosotros, el cual tenéis de Dios? No sois vuestros,
texts.1co.6.20: porque habéis sido comprados por un precio. Por tanto, glorificad a Dios en vuestro cuerpo y en vuestro espíritu, que son de Dios.
texts.1co.7.1: En cuanto a lo que me escribisteis, es bueno que el hombre no toque a la mujer.
texts.1co.7.2: Pero, a causa de las inmoralidades sexuales, que cada hombre tenga su propia esposa, y que cada mujer tenga su propio marido.
texts.1co.7.3: Que el marido dé a su mujer el afecto que se le debe, y así también la mujer a su marido.
texts.1co.7.4: La mujer no tiene autoridad sobre su propio cuerpo, sino el marido. Así también el marido no tiene autoridad sobre su propio cuerpo, sino la mujer.
texts.1co.7.5: No os privéis los unos a los otros, a no ser que sea de común acuerdo por un tiempo, para que os dediquéis al ayuno y a la oración, y estéis de nuevo juntos, para que Satanás no os tiente por vuestra falta de dominio propio.
texts.1co.7.6: Pero esto lo digo a modo de concesión, no de mandamiento.
texts.1co.7.7: Sin embargo, quisiera que todos los hombres fueran como yo. Sin embargo, cada hombre tiene su propio don de Dios, uno de este tipo y otro de aquel.
texts.1co.7.8: Pero a los solteros y a las viudas les digo que es bueno que se queden como yo.
texts.1co.7.9: Pero si no tienen dominio propio, que se casen. Porque es mejor casarse que arder de pasión.
texts.1co.7.10: Pero a los casados les ordeno, no yo, sino el Señor, que la mujer no deje a su marido
texts.1co.7.11: (pero si se separa, que se quede soltera, o que se reconcilie con su marido), y que el marido no deje a su mujer.
texts.1co.7.12: Pero a los demás, yo, no el Señor, os digo: Si algún hermano tiene una esposa incrédula, y ella se contenta con vivir con él, que no la deje.
texts.1co.7.13: La mujer que tiene un marido incrédulo, y éste se contenta con vivir con ella, que no deje a su marido.
texts.1co.7.14: Porque el marido incrédulo se santifica en la mujer, y la mujer incrédula se santifica en el marido. De lo contrario, vuestros hijos serían impuros, pero ahora son santos.
texts.1co.7.15: Pero si el incrédulo se aparta, que haya separación. El hermano o la hermana no están sometidos en tales casos, sino que Dios nos ha llamado en paz.
texts.1co.7.16: Pues ¿cómo sabes, esposa, si salvarás a tu marido? ¿O cómo sabes, esposo, si salvarás a tu esposa?
texts.1co.7.17: Solamente, como el Señor ha distribuido a cada hombre, como Dios ha llamado a cada uno, así debe caminar. Así lo ordeno en todas las asambleas.
texts.1co.7.18: ¿Se llamó a alguien habiendo sido circuncidado? Que no se vuelva incircunciso. ¿Ha sido llamado alguien en la incircuncisión? Que no se circuncide.
texts.1co.7.19: La circuncisión no es nada, y la incircuncisión no es nada, pero lo que importa es guardar los mandamientos de Dios.
texts.1co.7.20: Que cada uno permanezca en la vocación a la que fue llamado.
texts.1co.7.21: ¿Fuiste llamado siendo siervo? No dejes que eso te moleste, pero si tienes la oportunidad de ser libre, aprovéchala.
texts.1co.7.22: Porque el que fue llamado en el Señor siendo siervo, es el hombre libre del Señor. Asimismo, el que fue llamado siendo libre es siervo de Cristo.
texts.1co.7.23: Vosotros fuisteis comprados por un precio. No os hagáis siervos de los hombres.
texts.1co.7.24: Hermanos, que cada uno, en la condición en que fue llamado, permanezca en esa condición con Dios.
texts.1co.7.25: En cuanto a las vírgenes, no tengo ningún mandamiento del Señor, sino que doy mi juicio como alguien que ha obtenido la misericordia del Señor para ser digno de confianza.
texts.1co.7.26: Por lo tanto, creo que a causa de la angustia que nos invade, es bueno que el hombre permanezca como está.
texts.1co.7.27: ¿Estás atado a una esposa? No busques liberarte. ¿Estás libre de una esposa? No busques esposa.
texts.1co.7.28: Pero si te casas, no has pecado. Si una virgen se casa, no ha pecado. Sin embargo, los tales tendrán opresión en la carne, y yo quiero libraros.
texts.1co.7.29: Pero os digo esto, hermanos: el tiempo es corto. A partir de ahora, tanto los que tienen esposa como los que no la tienen;
texts.1co.7.30: y los que lloran, como si no lloraran; y los que se alegran, como si no se alegraran; y los que compran, como si no poseyeran;
texts.1co.7.31: y los que usan el mundo, como si no lo usaran al máximo. Porque el modo de este mundo pasa.
texts.1co.7.32: Pero yo quiero que estéis libres de preocupaciones. El que no está casado se preocupa de las cosas del Señor, de cómo puede agradar al Señor;
texts.1co.7.33: pero el que está casado se preocupa de las cosas del mundo, de cómo puede agradar a su mujer.
texts.1co.7.34: También hay una diferencia entre una esposa y una virgen. La mujer soltera se preocupa por las cosas del Señor, para ser santa tanto en cuerpo como en espíritu. Pero la que está casada se preocupa por las cosas del mundo: por complacer a su marido.
texts.1co.7.35: Esto lo digo por vuestro propio bien, no para tenderos un lazo, sino por lo que conviene, y para que atendáis al Señor sin distracción.
texts.1co.7.36: Pero si algún hombre piensa que se comporta de manera inapropiada con su virgen, si ella ha pasado la flor de la edad, y si la necesidad lo requiere, que haga lo que quiera. No peca. Que se casen.
texts.1co.7.37: Pero el que se mantiene firme en su corazón, sin tener urgencia, sino que tiene poder sobre su propia voluntad, y ha decidido en su propio corazón conservar su propia virgen, hace bien.
texts.1co.7.38: Así pues, tanto el que da su propia virgen en matrimonio hace bien, como el que no la da en matrimonio hace mejor.
texts.1co.7.39: La mujer está obligada por la ley mientras viva su marido; pero si el marido ha muerto, es libre de casarse con quien quiera, sólo en el Señor.
texts.1co.7.40: Pero ella es más feliz si se queda como está, a mi juicio, y creo que también tengo el Espíritu de Dios.
